title.en: Volume 300 Biographies 188: Families of Imperial Consorts

sentences.zh: 明太祖立國，家法嚴。

translations.literal: When Taizu of Ming founded the state, the household regulations were strict.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor founded the Ming dynasty, his household code was strict.

sentences.zh: 史臣稱後妃居宮中，不預一發之政，外戚循理謹度，無敢恃寵以病民，漢、唐以來所不及。

translations.literal: The historiographer states that empresses and consorts dwelling in the palace did not participate in the slightest matter of government; maternal relatives followed reason and observed propriety, none daring to rely on favor to harm the people—something unmatched since Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write that palace consorts took no part whatever in governance, while affinal kin observed the rules and kept their distance, none presuming on imperial favor to oppress the people—a record unmatched since the Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 而高、文二後賢明，抑遠外氏。

translations.literal: Moreover, the two empresses of Gao and Wen were wise and enlightened, restraining and keeping distant the maternal clans.
translations.idiomatic: The empresses of Hongwu and Yongle were especially wise and deliberately kept their kinsmen at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 太祖訪得高後親族，將授以官。

translations.literal: Taizu inquired and found relatives of the Gao empress, and was about to grant them offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu tracked down kinsmen of Empress Ma and prepared to give them posts,

sentences.zh: 後謝曰：「國家爵祿，宜與賢士大夫共之，不當私妾家。」

translations.literal: the empress declined, saying: "The state's ranks and stipends ought to be shared with worthy scholar-officials; they should not be monopolized by my own family as a concubine's kin.
translations.idiomatic: the empress refused: "State honors ought to be shared with worthy scholar-officials, not reserved for my own clan.

sentences.zh: 且援前世外戚驕佚致禍為辭。

translations.literal: She moreover cited as her reason the arrogance and indulgence of maternal relatives in previous ages bringing disaster.
translations.idiomatic: She cited the disasters wrought by arrogant affinal kin in earlier dynasties as her reason.

sentences.zh: 帝善后言，賜金帛而已。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the empress's words and gave only gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved her counsel and rewarded her kin with gold and silk alone.

sentences.zh: 定國之封，文皇后謂非己誌，臨終猶勸帝，毋驕畜外家。

translations.literal: Regarding enfeoffment for Dingguo, the Wen empress said it was not her wish; on her deathbed she still admonished the emperor not to pamper and shelter the maternal clan.
translations.idiomatic: When enfeoffments for the Xuande era were proposed, Empress Xu said they ran counter to her wishes and on her deathbed still urged the emperor not to indulge his wife's kin.

sentences.zh: 詒謀既遠，宗社奠安，而椒房貴戚亦藉以保福慶逮子孫，所全不已多乎。

translations.literal: The counsels left for posterity being far-reaching, the altars of state were settled in peace, and the noble kin of the inner quarters also thereby preserved blessings reaching their descendants—how many were they not thereby preserved!
translations.idiomatic: With such far-sighted policy the dynasty was secured, and imperial in-laws too were spared to pass on their good fortune to posterity—how many lives and houses were thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 惟英宗時，會昌侯孫繼宗以奪門功，參議國是。

translations.literal: Only in the time of Emperor Yingzong did Marquis of Huichang Sun Jizong, by merit in the coup of the Gate Incident, participate in deliberating state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Yingzong did Sun Jizong, Marquis of Huichang, parlay his role in restoring the throne into a voice in statecraft.

sentences.zh: 自茲以下，其賢者類多謹身奉法，謙謙有儒者風。

translations.literal: From this time downward, the worthy among them mostly were careful in person and observed the law, modest with the bearing of Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the better sort were for the most part scrupulous and law-abiding, with the modest bearing of literati.

sentences.zh: 而一二怙恩負乘之徒，所好不過田宅、狗馬、音樂，所狎不過俳優、伎妾，非有軍國之權，賓客朋黨之勢。

translations.literal: But the one or two who relied on favor and rode on momentum—their pleasures were no more than estates, dogs and horses, and music; their intimates no more than actors, jesters, and courtesans; they had no power over armies and state, no force of retainers and factions.
translations.idiomatic: A few who traded on grace amused themselves with estates, horses, and music, and with players and concubines—but held no military power and built no factions.

sentences.zh: 而在廷諸臣好為危言激論，汰如壽寧兄弟，庸駑如鄭國泰，已逐影尋聲，抨擊不遺余力。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers at court delighted in startling words and heated argument; even toward mediocrities like the Shouning brothers, or dolts like Zheng Guotai, they would follow shadow and sound, attacking without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers nevertheless loved alarmist rhetoric: mediocrities like the Shouning brothers or dullards like Zheng Guotai were hunted on the slightest rumor and assailed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 故有明一代，外戚最為孱弱。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the one Ming age, maternal relatives were weakest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for the whole Ming period affinal power was uniquely feeble.

sentences.zh: 然而惠安、新樂，舉宗殉國，嗚呼卓矣！

translations.literal: Yet Huian and Xingle—whole clans dying for the state—ah, how eminent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the houses of Huian and Xingle died to a man for the dynasty—truly noble!

sentences.zh: 成祖後家，詳《中山王傳》，余采其行事可紀者，作《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: The empress's family of Chengzu is detailed in the "Biography of the Prince of Zhongshan"; I gather their deeds worth recording and compose this "Biography of Maternal Relatives."
translations.idiomatic: Yongle's consort kin are treated in the biography of the Prince of Zhongshan; here I collect what is worth recording among the rest for this chapter on imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 陳公，逸其名，淳皇后父也。

translations.literal: Lord Chen, his personal name lost, was father of Empress Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Chen, whose given name is lost, was the father of Empress Chun.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年追封揚王，媼為王夫人，立祠太廟東。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yang; his wife as Lady of the Prince, and a shrine was established east of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 1369 he was posthumously made Prince of Yang and his wife Lady of the Prince; a shrine was erected east of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 明年有言王墓在盱眙者，中都守臣按之信。

translations.literal: The next year someone reported that the prince's tomb was at Xuyi; the guardian official of the central capital investigated and found it true.
translations.idiomatic: The following year it was reported that the prince's tomb lay at Xuyi; the official sent to investigate confirmed it.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命中書省即墓次立廟，設祠祭署，奉祀一人，守墓戶二百一十家，世世復。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the Secretariat to erect a temple at the tomb site, establish a sacrificial office, appoint one attendant sacrificer, and assign two hundred and ten households to guard the tomb, exempted in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered a temple built at the graveside, with a sacrificial office, one officiant, and two hundred and ten hereditary tomb-guard households forever exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 帝自制《揚王行實》，諭翰林學士宋濂文其碑，略曰：

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed the "Conduct of Prince Yang" and instructed Hanlin Academician Song Lian to compose the text for his stele, which in summary says:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself wrote an account of Prince Yang's life and directed Hanlin Academician Song Lian to compose the stele inscription, which in summary reads:

sentences.zh: 王姓陳氏，世維揚人，不知其諱。

translations.literal: The prince's surname was Chen; his family for generations were people of Weiyang; his taboo name is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was surnamed Chen, a native of the Yangzhou region for generations; his personal name is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 當宋季，名隸尺籍伍符中，從大將張世傑扈從祥興。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, his name was registered in the military rolls; he followed the great general Zhang Shijie in attending Emperor Xiangxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of the Song his name was entered on the military rolls; he followed the general Zhang Shijie in the entourage of the boy emperor Bing.

sentences.zh: 至元己卯春，世傑與元兵戰，師大潰，士卒多溺死。

translations.literal: In the spring of the jimao year of Zhiyuan, Zhang Shijie fought the Yuan army; the army was utterly routed and many soldiers drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1339 Zhang Shijie fought the Yuan forces; his army was shattered and countless men drowned.

sentences.zh: 王幸脫死達岸，與一二同行者，累石支破釜，煮遺糧以療饑。

translations.literal: The prince fortunately escaped death and reached shore; with one or two companions he piled stones to prop up a broken cauldron and cooked leftover grain to relieve hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The prince barely reached shore alive; with one or two companions he propped a broken pot on stones and boiled scraps of grain to stave off starvation.

sentences.zh: 已而絕糧，同行者聞山有死馬，將其烹食之。

translations.literal: Soon grain ran out; his companions heard there was a dead horse on the mountain and were about to cook and eat it.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain was gone, his companions heard of a dead horse on the hill and prepared to cook it.

sentences.zh: 王疲極晝睡，夢一白衣人來曰：「汝慎勿食馬肉，今夜有舟來共載也。」

translations.literal: The prince, utterly exhausted, slept by day and dreamed a man in white came saying: "Take care not to eat horse flesh; tonight a boat will come to carry you together.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted, the prince fell asleep by day and dreamed that a man in white said, "Do not eat the horse meat—a boat will come tonight to take you away.

sentences.zh: 王未之深信，俄又夢如初。

translations.literal: The prince did not fully believe it; soon he dreamed again as before.
translations.idiomatic: He did not fully believe it, but soon dreamed the same dream again.

sentences.zh: 至夜將半，夢中仿佛聞櫓聲，有衣紫衣者以杖觸王胯曰：「舟至矣。」

translations.literal: Near midnight he seemed in his dream to hear the sound of oars; a man in purple garments touched the prince's hip with a staff, saying: "The boat has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Near midnight he seemed to hear oars in his sleep; a man in purple tapped his hip with a staff and said, "The boat is here.

sentences.zh: 王驚寤，身已在舟上，見舊所事統領官。

translations.literal: The prince started awake in alarm and found himself already on a boat, seeing the commander officer he had formerly served.
translations.idiomatic: He woke with a start to find himself already aboard a boat with the officer he had once served under.

sentences.zh: 時統領已降於元將，元將令來附者輒擲棄水中。

translations.literal: At that time the commander had already surrendered to the Yuan general, who ordered that those who came to submit be thrown into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had already surrendered to a Yuan general who ordered every defector thrown overboard.

sentences.zh: 統領憐王，藏之艎板下，日取乾糇從板隙投之，王掬以食。

translations.literal: The commander pitied the prince and hid him beneath the deck planks; each day he took dry provisions and cast them through gaps in the planks, and the prince scooped them up to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying him, the commander hid him under the deck and each day dropped dry rations through the cracks for him to scoop up and eat.

sentences.zh: 復與王約，以足撼板，王即張口從板隙受漿。

translations.literal: He also made an agreement with the prince: when he kicked the planks, the prince would open his mouth and receive gruel through the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed that when the commander kicked the planks the prince would open his mouth to receive broth through the cracks.

sentences.zh: 居數日，事泄，仿徨不自安。

translations.literal: After several days the matter leaked out, and he wandered in distress, unable to be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the secret was discovered and he was left in anguished uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 颶風吹舟，盤旋如轉輪，久不能進，元將大恐。

translations.literal: A typhoon blew the boat, whirling it like a wheel; for long it could not advance, and the Yuan general was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A typhoon spun the boat like a wheel and held it fast for days, filling the Yuan commander with dread.

sentences.zh: 統領知王善巫術，遂白而出之。

translations.literal: The commander knew the prince was skilled in shaman arts and so reported and had him brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the prince practiced divination, the commander reported him and had him brought out.

sentences.zh: 王仰天叩齒，若指麾鬼神狀，風濤頓息。

translations.literal: The prince looked up to heaven and clicked his teeth as if directing spirits; wind and waves instantly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The prince gazed skyward and chattered his teeth as though commanding spirits, and the storm fell still at once.

sentences.zh: 元將喜，因飲食之。

translations.literal: The Yuan general rejoiced and therefore gave him drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan commander was delighted and gave him food and drink.

sentences.zh: 至通州，送之登岸。

translations.literal: When they reached Tongzhou, they sent him ashore.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou they put him ashore.

sentences.zh: 王歸維揚，不樂為軍伍，避去盱眙津裏鎮，以巫術行。

translations.literal: The prince returned to Weiyang, disliking military service; he withdrew to Jinli Town in Xuyi and made his living by shaman arts.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Yangzhou region, left the army, and settled at Jinli in Xuyi, earning his living as a diviner.

sentences.zh: 王無子，生二女，長適季氏，次即皇太后。

translations.literal: The prince had no son; he bore two daughters—the elder married the Ji clan, the younger became the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons but two daughters: the elder married into the Ji family, the younger became the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 晚以季氏長子為後，年九十九薨，遂葬焉，今墓是已。

translations.literal: In his old age he took the Ji clan's eldest son as heir; at age ninety-nine he died and was buried there—this is the present tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he adopted the Ji family's eldest son as heir; he died at ninety-nine and was buried there—the present tomb.

sentences.zh: 臣濂聞君子之制行，能感於人固難，而能通於神明為尤難。

translations.literal: Your subject Lian has heard that for a gentleman's conduct to move people is already difficult, but to communicate with the spirits is especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Lian observes that for a gentleman's conduct to move others is rare enough, but to move the spirits is rarer still.

sentences.zh: 今當患難危急之時，神假夢寐，挾以升舟，非精誠上通於天，何以致神人之佑至於斯也。

translations.literal: Now at a time of peril and crisis, the spirits used dreams to lift him onto a boat—had not sincerity penetrated to Heaven, how could divine and human aid reach such a point?
translations.idiomatic: In mortal peril the spirits spoke through dreams and lifted him onto a boat—without sincerity reaching Heaven, how could divine aid come so far?

sentences.zh: 舉此推之，則積德之深厚，斷可信矣。

translations.literal: Inferring from this, the depth of accumulated virtue may surely be believed.
translations.idiomatic: From this one may surely believe how deep his accumulated virtue ran.

sentences.zh: 是宜慶鐘聖女，誕育皇上，以啟億萬年無疆之基，於乎盛哉！

translations.literal: It was fitting that blessed fortune should gather on a holy daughter, who bore the emperor and opened the foundation of boundless myriad years—ah, how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: No wonder blessed fortune gathered on his holy daughter, who bore the emperor and laid the foundation of an endless dynasty—how glorious!

sentences.zh: 臣濂既序其事，復再拜稽首而獻銘曰：皇帝建國，克展孝思。

translations.literal: Your subject Lian, having narrated these events, again bowed twice and touched his forehead to the ground and presented an inscription, saying: The emperor founded the state and was able to display filial thought.
translations.idiomatic: Having narrated these events, your servant Lian bowed again and offered this inscription: The emperor founded the realm and fulfilled his filial duty.

sentences.zh: 疏封母族，自親而推。

translations.literal: He extended enfeoffment to the maternal clan, proceeding from those nearest.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled his mother's kin, extending honor from those closest.

sentences.zh: 錫爵維揚，地邇帝畿，立廟崇祀，玄冕袞衣。

translations.literal: He bestowed a title in Weiyang, the land near the imperial domain; he erected a temple for lofty sacrifice, with dark caps and dragon robes.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a title in Yangzhou, near the capital, raised a temple for solemn rites, and robed the spirit in imperial vestments.

sentences.zh: 痛念宅兆，卜之何墟，閭師來告，今在盱眙。

translations.literal: Grieving for the burial ground, he divined what mound—village elders came to report: it is now at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Longing for his forebear's grave, he sought its site; village elders came to say it lay at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 皇情悅豫，繼以涕洟，即詔禮官，汝往葺治，毋俾蕘豎，跳踉以嬉。

translations.literal: The imperial heart was pleased, then followed by tears and mucus; he immediately commanded the ritual officials: "You go and repair it; do not let rustic lads leap and play upon it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced, then wept, and at once charged the ritual officers: "Go and restore it; let no rustic boys trample it in sport."

sentences.zh: 惟我揚王，昔隸戎麾，獰風蕩海，糧絕阻饑。

translations.literal: Our Prince of Yang of old served under military banners; fierce winds swept the sea, grain ran out and hunger blocked his way.
translations.idiomatic: Our Prince of Yang once served in the armies; fierce winds lashed the sea, grain failed, and hunger barred his path.

sentences.zh: 天有顯相，夢來紫衣，挾以登舟，神力所持，易死為生，壽躋期頤。

translations.literal: Heaven showed a clear sign: in dreams came one in purple, who lifted him onto a boat; divine power sustained him, turning death into life, his years reaching a full span.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven showed its favor: a man in purple came in dreams and lifted him aboard; divine power turned death to life and gave him a full span of years.

sentences.zh: 積累深長，未究厥施，乃毓聖女，茂衍皇支。

translations.literal: Accumulated merit was deep and long; its full reward was not yet exhausted—then he nurtured a holy daughter, who richly extended the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ran deep and long, its reward not yet spent—until he nurtured a holy daughter who richly extended the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 蘿圖肇開，鴻祚峨巍，日照月臨，風行霆馳。

translations.literal: The vine-chart was first opened, great fortune towered high; sun shone and moon looked down, wind moved and thunder raced.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial line was opened, great fortune rose high; sun and moon looked down, wind and thunder raced.

sentences.zh: 自流徂源，功亦有歸，無德弗酬，典禮可稽。

translations.literal: From the stream trace back to the source—merit too has its return; none without virtue goes unrewarded; ritual norms may be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: From the stream one traces the source—merit too finds its reward; no virtue goes unpaid; ritual precedent stands firm.

sentences.zh: 聿昭化原，扶植政基，以廣孝治，以惇民彜。

translations.literal: Thus the transforming origin is made bright, the governmental foundation is upheld, filial governance is broadened, and the people's constant norms are deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the source of transformation is made clear, the foundation of rule upheld, filial governance extended, and the people's customs secured.

sentences.zh: 津裏之鎮，王靈所依，於昭萬年，視此銘詩。

translations.literal: Jinli Town is where the prince's spirit relies; for ten thousand bright years, behold this inscribed verse.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinli Town his spirit rests; for ten thousand years may this inscription stand.

sentences.zh: 馬公，逸其名，高皇后父也，宿州人。

translations.literal: Lord Ma, his personal name lost, was father of the Gao empress, a man of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ma, whose given name is lost, was the father of Empress Ma and a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 元末殺人，亡命定遠。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he killed a man and fled for his life to Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he killed a man and fled to Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 與郭子興善，以季女屬子興，後歸太祖，即高皇后也。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Guo Zixing and entrusted his youngest daughter to Zixing; she later married Taizu—this was the Gao empress.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Guo Zixing and gave him his youngest daughter in marriage; she later wed Taizu and became Empress Ma.

sentences.zh: 公及妻鄭媼皆前卒，洪武二年追封徐王，媼為王夫人，建祠太廟東。

translations.literal: The lord and his wife Lady Zheng had both died earlier; in the second year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, she as Lady of the Prince, and a shrine was built east of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife Lady Zheng had died earlier; in 1369 he was posthumously made Prince of Xu and she Lady of the Prince, with a shrine east of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 皇后親奉安神主，祝文稱「孝女皇后馬氏，謹奉皇帝命致祭。」

translations.literal: The empress personally presented the spirit tablet for installation; the prayer text read: "The filial daughter Empress Ma, reverently receiving the emperor's command, performs the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The empress herself installed the spirit tablet; the prayer read, "Filial daughter Empress Ma, by the emperor's command, offers this sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 四年命禮部尚書陶凱即宿州塋次立廟，帝自為文以祭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he ordered Minister of Rites Tao Kai to erect a temple at the Suzhou grave site; the emperor himself composed a text for the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1371 he ordered Minister of Rites Tao Kai to build a temple at the Suzhou graveside, and composed the sacrificial text himself.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「朕惟古者創業之君，必得賢後以為內助，共定大業。

translations.literal: The text says: "We consider that ancient founders of states must obtain worthy consorts as inner aid to settle the great enterprise together.
translations.idiomatic: The text reads: "I reflect that founders of old needed worthy consorts as partners within to secure the realm together.

sentences.zh: 及天下已安，必追崇外家，以報其德。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven was already at peace, they necessarily honored the maternal clan posthumously to repay their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was at peace, they always honored the consort's kin to repay their merit.

sentences.zh: 惟外舅、外姑實生賢女，正位中宮。

translations.literal: Our maternal uncle and aunt truly bore a worthy daughter who took the central palace position.
translations.idiomatic: My wife's father and mother bore a worthy daughter who took her place in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 朕既追封外舅為徐王，外姑為王夫人，以王無繼嗣，立廟京師，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: We have already posthumously enfeoffed our maternal uncle as Prince of Xu and our maternal aunt as Lady of the Prince; since the prince had no heir, we established a temple in the capital and perform seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: I have enfeoffed my wife's father as Prince of Xu and her mother as Lady of the Prince; as the prince left no heir, I raised a temple in the capital for seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 然稽之古典，於禮未安。

translations.literal: Yet consulting ancient models, in ritual this is not proper.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by ancient precedent this was not ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 又念人生其土，魂魄必遊故鄉，故即塋所立廟，俾有司春秋奉祀。

translations.literal: We also reflect that one is born on one's native soil and the soul-spirit must roam the old home; therefore we establish a temple at the grave site and charge officials to perform spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that the soul returns to its native soil, I have built a temple at the grave and charged officials to sacrifice in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 茲擇吉辰，遣禮官奉安神主於新廟，靈其昭格，尚鑒在茲。」

translations.literal: Now selecting an auspicious day, we dispatch ritual officials to install the spirit tablet in the new temple—may the spirit brightly descend; may it regard this."
translations.idiomatic: On this auspicious day I send ritual officers to install the spirit tablet in the new temple—may your spirit descend and witness this."

sentences.zh: 二十五年設祠祭署，奉祀、祀丞各一人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year a sacrificial office was established, with one attendant sacrificer and one assistant sacrificer each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1392 a sacrificial office was established with one chief and one assistant officiant.

sentences.zh: 王無後，以外親武忠、武聚為之，置灑掃戶九十三家。

translations.literal: The prince had no descendants; maternal relatives Wu Zhong and Wu Ju were appointed in his stead, and ninety-three households were assigned for sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the prince left no heir, affinal kin Wu Zhong and Wu Ju were appointed, with ninety-three households for tomb maintenance.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年北巡，親謁祠下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, on the northern tour, he personally visited the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On his northern tour in 1409 the Yongle Emperor visited the shrine in person.

sentences.zh: 守冢武戡為建陽衛鎮撫，犯法，責而宥之。

translations.literal: Tomb guardian Wu Kan was garrison commander of Jianyang Guard; he violated the law and was rebuked but pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb guardian Wu Kan, a battalion commander of Jianyang Guard, broke the law and was rebuked but pardoned.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝復親祭，以戡為徐州衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor again sacrificed in person and made Kan assistant commander of Xuzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1417 the emperor sacrificed in person again and made Kan assistant commander of Xuzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 呂本，壽州人，懿文太子次妃父也。

translations.literal: Lü Ben was a man of Shouzhou, father of the secondary consort of Crown Prince Yiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ben of Shouzhou was the father of Crown Prince Yiwen's secondary consort.

sentences.zh: 仕元，為元帥府都事。

translations.literal: He served the Yuan as chief clerk of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan he served as chief clerk of a marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後歸太祖，授中書省令史。

translations.literal: Later he submitted to Taizu and was appointed clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to Taizu and was made a clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年歷官吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu he served as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1372 he served as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年改太常司卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1373 he was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，御史臺言：「本奉職不謹，郊壇牲角非繭栗，功臣廟壞不修。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year the Censorate reported: "Ben in performing his duties was not careful—the horns of suburban altar victims were not fine and tight, and the shrine of meritorious ministers was ruined without repair.
translations.idiomatic: The following April the Censorate reported that Ben had been negligent: suburban sacrifice victims' horns were not properly formed, and the shrine of meritorious ministers lay in disrepair.

sentences.zh: 詔免官，罰役功臣廟。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed him from office and punished him with labor on the shrine of meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and sentenced to labor repairing the shrine of meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 已，釋為北平按察司僉事。

translations.literal: Later he was released and made Vice Commissioner of the Beiping Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was later released and appointed vice commissioner of the Beiping surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 帝召本及同時被命楊基、答祿與權，諭之曰：「風憲之設，在肅紀綱，清吏治，非專理刑名。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ben, together with Yang Ji, Dalu Yuquan, and others appointed at the same time, and instructed them, saying: "The establishment of censorial overseers is to maintain discipline and statutes and to cleanse official governance—it is not solely to administer criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Lü Ben, along with Yang Ji, Dalu Yuquan, and the others appointed at the same time, and instructed them: "Censorial offices exist to uphold discipline and purify governance, not merely to handle criminal matters.

sentences.zh: 爾等往修厥職，務明大體，毋效俗吏拘繩墨。

translations.literal: You shall go and fulfill your duties, striving to grasp the broader principles; do not imitate petty officials bound by the letter of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Go and perform your duties, keeping the larger picture in view—do not imitate petty officials rigidly bound by statutes and rules.

sentences.zh: 善雖小，為之不已，將成全德；

translations.literal: Though good may be small, if pursued without cease it will form a complete virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Though a virtue be small, pursued without end it will become full excellence;

sentences.zh: 過雖小，積之不已，將為大憝。

translations.literal: Though faults may be small, if accumulated without cease they will become great evils.
translations.idiomatic: though a fault be small, accumulated without end it will become great wickedness.

sentences.zh: 不見幹雲之臺，由寸土之積，燎原之火，由一爝之微，可不慎哉！」

translations.literal: Does one not see that the platform reaching the clouds comes from the accumulation of inch upon inch of earth, and that a fire sweeping the plains comes from the tiny spark of a single torch? How can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you not see that a platform reaching the clouds is built inch by inch, and a fire that burns the plain begins with a single spark? How can you not be on your guard!

sentences.zh: 本等頓首受命，尋復累遷太常司卿。

translations.literal: Ben and the others kowtowed to receive the command. Soon he was again promoted through successive ranks to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ben and the others kowtowed to accept the charge. Before long he was promoted again, in successive steps, to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 逾二年卒，無子，賜葬鐘山之陰。

translations.literal: After more than two years he died. He had no son, and was granted burial on the northern slope of Mount Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: A little over two years later he died. He had no son and was granted burial on the northern slope of Mount Zhong.

sentences.zh: 馬全，洪武中為光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Ma Quan served in the Hongwu era as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quan served under Hongwu as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 其女，乃惠帝后也。

translations.literal: His daughter was empress to Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was Empress to the Jianwen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 燕兵陷都城，全不知所終。

translations.literal: When the Yan army captured the capital, Quan's fate became unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan armies took the capital, Quan vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 昶從成祖起兵取大寧，戰鄭村壩，俱有功，授義勇中衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: Chang Sheng followed the Chengzu Emperor in raising troops, captured Daning, and fought at Zheng Village Dam—all with merit—and was appointed Vice Commander of the Yiyong Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Sheng followed the Yongle Emperor in arms, helped take Daning, and fought at Zheng Village Dam with distinction; he was made vice commander of the Yiyong Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 已，援蘇州，敗遼東軍，還佐世子守北平。

translations.literal: Afterward he reinforced Suzhou, defeated the Liaodong army, and returned to assist the Heir Apparent in defending Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to relieve Suzhou, routed the Liaodong forces, and returned to help the heir apparent hold Beiping.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，累官錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he rose through successive posts to Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he rose through the ranks to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 昶嘗有過，成祖戒之曰：「戚畹最當守法，否則罪倍常人。

translations.literal: Chang Sheng once committed an offense. The Chengzu Emperor admonished him, saying: "As affinal kin you above all must obey the law; otherwise your guilt will be double that of ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Sheng once transgressed, the Yongle Emperor warned him: "As imperial in-laws you above all must keep the law—otherwise your guilt will be twice that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 汝今富貴，能不忘貧賤，驕逸何自生。

translations.literal: You are now rich and noble; if you can remember poverty and low station, from what will arrogance and dissipation arise?
translations.idiomatic: You are wealthy and exalted now; if you never forget your humble beginnings, how can arrogance or indulgence take root?

sentences.zh: 若奢傲放縱，陵虐下人，必不爾恕，慎之。」

translations.literal: If you are luxurious, proud, and unrestrained, bullying and abusing your subordinates, I shall certainly not forgive you—be careful."
translations.idiomatic: But if you grow extravagant, haughty, and unrestrained, and bully those beneath you, I will not pardon you. Take care.

sentences.zh: 昶頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chang Sheng kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Sheng kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，擢中軍都督府左都督，俄封彭城伯，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended, he was promoted to Left Commander-in-Chief of the Central Military Commission; soon he was enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongxi Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to left commander-in-chief of the Central Military Commission and soon enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng, the title to pass to his heirs.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，命掌五軍右哨軍馬。

translations.literal: When the Hongxi reign title was adopted, he was ordered to take charge of the horses of the Right Ward of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongxi reign was proclaimed, he was placed in charge of the cavalry of the Five Armies' right ward.

sentences.zh: 英宗嗣位，年幼，太皇太后召昶兄弟誡諭之，凡朝政弗令預。

translations.literal: When Yingzong succeeded, still young, the Grand Empress Dowager summoned Chang Sheng and his brothers and admonished them, forbidding them any participation in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded as a child, the grand empress dowager summoned Chang Sheng and his brothers and warned them not to involve themselves in court policy.

sentences.zh: 昶兄弟素恭謹，因訓飭益自斂。

translations.literal: Chang Sheng and his brothers had always been respectful and cautious; admonished thus, they restrained themselves all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers had always been deferential and careful; after this admonition they held themselves in all the more.

sentences.zh: 正統三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1438.

sentences.zh: 長子輔病廢，子瑾嗣。

translations.literal: The eldest son Fu was disabled by illness; Jin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fu was invalided by illness, and Jin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 以伯爵封輔，命未下而輔卒。

translations.literal: Fu was to be enfeoffed as an earl, but before the order was issued he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was to receive an earldom, but the patent had not yet been issued when he died.

sentences.zh: 初，昶私蓄奄人，瑾匿不舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chang Sheng had privately kept eunuchs; Jin concealed this and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chang Sheng had secretly kept eunuchs in his household; Jin hid the fact and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 事發，下獄，已，獲釋。

translations.literal: When the matter came out, he was imprisoned; later he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came to light he was imprisoned, but was later released.

sentences.zh: 瑾從弟玘，天順中，官錦衣衛副千戶。

translations.literal: Jin's younger cousin Qi, in the Tianshun era, held the post of Deputy Company Commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger cousin Qi served in the Tianshun era as deputy company commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 飲千戶呂宏家，醉抽刀刺宏死，法當斬，有司援議親末滅。

translations.literal: Drinking at the home of Company Commander Lü Hong, he drunkenly drew a knife and stabbed Hong to death. By law he deserved execution; the officials invoked deliberation on close kin to reduce the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: While drinking at the home of company commander Lü Hong, he drunkenly drew a knife and killed him. By law he merited execution, but the officials urged mitigation under the deliberation for imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 詔不從，迄如律。

translations.literal: An edict refused this; in the end the law was applied as written.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and in the end the sentence was carried out according to law.

sentences.zh: 成化十六年，瑾卒，子信嗣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chenghua, Jin died; his son Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1480 Jin died, and his son Xin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 其後裔嗣封，見《世表》。

translations.literal: Their descendants' successive enfeoffments are recorded in the Genealogical Tables.
translations.idiomatic: The line's later inheritances are set out in the Genealogical Tables.

sentences.zh: 子鑭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十年，言官劾勛戚權豪家置店房、科私稅諸罪，鑭亦預，輸贖還爵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, censorial officials impeached meritorious nobles, the powerful, and great houses for crimes such as maintaining shops and levying private taxes; Lan was also implicated, paid a redemption fine, and had his title restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, remonstrating officials impeached ennobled kin and mighty houses for keeping shops, collecting illegal levies, and related offenses; Lan was among them, paid a fine to redeem his rank, and was restored to his title.

sentences.zh: 二十七年掌後府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he managed affairs of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he took charge of the rear military commission.

sentences.zh: 居三年卒。

translations.literal: After three years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 子元善嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuanshan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanshan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年僉書後府事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he served as assistant director of the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1570 he was appointed assistant director of the rear military commission.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the thirty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1609.

sentences.zh: 子慶臻嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qingzhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingzhen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 四十八年掌左府事。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he managed affairs of the Left Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he took charge of the left military commission.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年七月命提督京營。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Chongzhen he was ordered to supervise the Capital Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1628 he was appointed to supervise the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 慶臻私請內閣，於敕內增入兼管捕營。

translations.literal: Qingzhen privately petitioned the Grand Secretariat to add to the patent that he should also oversee the Pacification Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhen privately asked the Grand Secretariat to insert into his commission that he would also oversee the Pacification Battalion.

sentences.zh: 捕營提督鄭其心訐慶臻侵職，帝怒，詰改敕故。

translations.literal: Zheng Qixin, supervisor of the Pacification Battalion, denounced Qingzhen for encroaching on his duties; the emperor was angry and demanded the reason the patent had been altered.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qixin, who supervised the Pacification Battalion, accused Qingzhen of overstepping his post; the emperor was furious and demanded why the commission had been altered.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉鴻訓至遣戍，慶臻以世臣停祿三年。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun was banished to the frontier; Qingzhen, as a hereditary minister, had his salary suspended for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun was sent into exile; Qingzhen, as a hereditary courtier, had his stipend suspended for three years.

sentences.zh: 後復起，掌都督府。

translations.literal: Later he was restored to office and managed the Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored and put in charge of the military commission.

sentences.zh: 十七年，賊陷都城，慶臻召親黨盡散貲財，闔家自燔死。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when bandits captured the capital, Qingzhen summoned his kin and clansmen, distributed all his wealth, and the whole household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1644, when rebels took the capital, Qingzhen gathered his kin, gave away his entire fortune, and his whole household died by self-immolation.

sentences.zh: 南渡時，贈太師、惠安侯，謚忠武，合祀旌忠祠。

translations.literal: At the time of the southern crossing he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Marquis of Huian, given the posthumous title Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial), and jointly enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south he was posthumously made grand preceptor and Marquis of Huian, with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial, and honored together in the Shrine of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗嘉靖八年革外戚世爵，惟彭城、惠安獲存，慶臻卒殉國難。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the eighth year of Jiajing under the Shizong Emperor, hereditary titles for affinal kin were abolished; only Pengcheng and Huian were preserved—and Qingzhen ultimately died martyred for the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 1529 the Jiajing Emperor had abolished hereditary peerages for affinal kin, sparing only Pengcheng and Huian; Qingzhen in the end gave his life in the dynastic crisis.

sentences.zh: 胡榮，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Hu Rong was a man of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Rong was from Jining.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，長女入宮為女官，授錦衣衛百戶。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era his eldest daughter entered the palace as a palace lady; he was granted the post of Company Commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu his eldest daughter entered the palace as a female official, and he was given a company commandership in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年將冊其第三女為皇太孫妃，擢光祿寺卿，子安為府軍前衛指揮僉事，專侍太孫，不蒞事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yongle, when his third daughter was about to be installed as consort to the Grand Heir Apparent, he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his son An was made Assistant Commander of the Forward Military Guard of the Imperial Bodyguard, attending exclusively on the Grand Heir Apparent without assuming regular duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1417, as his third daughter was to be invested as consort to the heir apparent, he was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his son An was made assistant commander of the Forward Military Guard of the Imperial Bodyguard to attend the heir apparent exclusively, without taking up regular duties.

sentences.zh: 後太孫踐阼，妃為皇后，安亦屢進官。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Heir Apparent ascended the throne; the consort became empress, and An was repeatedly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent later ascended the throne and his daughter became empress, An too was promoted repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，後廢，胡氏遂不振。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande the empress was deposed, and the Hu clan thereafter declined.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was deposed in 1428, the Hu family never recovered its standing.

sentences.zh: 孫忠，字主敬，鄒平人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhong, styled Zhujing, was a man of Zouping.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhong, styled Zhujing, was a native of Zouping.

sentences.zh: 初名愚，宣宗改曰忠。

translations.literal: His original name was Yu; the Xuande Emperor changed it to Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Yu; the Xuande Emperor renamed him Zhong.

sentences.zh: 初，以永城主簿督夫營天壽山陵，有勞，遷鴻臚寺序班，選其女入皇太孫宮。

translations.literal: Earlier, as registrar of Yongcheng he supervised laborers in building the Tianshou Mountain tomb and had merit; he was transferred to Attendant of the Court of Imperial Banquets, and his daughter was selected for the Grand Heir Apparent's palace.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as registrar of Yongcheng, supervising corvée labor on the Tianshou Mountain tomb with credit; he was promoted to attendant of the Court of Imperial Banquets, and his daughter was chosen for the heir apparent's inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，冊貴妃，授忠中軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor ascended, the consort was enfeoffed as Noble Consort and Zhong was granted Vice Commissioner of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuande took the throne, his daughter was made noble consort and Zhong was given a vice commissionership in the central military command.

sentences.zh: 三年，皇后胡氏廢，貴妃為皇后，封忠會昌伯。

translations.literal: In the third year Empress Hu was deposed, the Noble Consort became empress, and Zhong was enfeoffed as Earl of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Empress Hu was deposed, his daughter became empress, and Zhong was enfeoffed as Earl of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁告歸裏，禦制詩賜之，命中官輔行。

translations.literal: Once when he requested leave to return home, the emperor composed a poem in his own hand and bestowed it, ordering a eunuch to accompany him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When he once asked leave to visit home, the emperor composed a poem himself as a gift and sent a eunuch to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 比還，帝後臨幸慰勞。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor and empress personally visited to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor and empress came in person to visit and reward him.

sentences.zh: 妻董夫人數召入宮，賜賫弗絕。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Dong was repeatedly summoned to the palace and gifts were bestowed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Dong, was summoned to the palace again and again, and gifts never stopped.

sentences.zh: 正統中，皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era the empress became empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era his daughter became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 忠生日，太后使使賜其家。

translations.literal: On Zhong's birthday the empress dowager sent envoys with gifts to his household.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhong's birthday the empress dowager sent envoys with gifts to his home.

sentences.zh: 時王振專權，祭酒李時勉荷校國學門，忠附奏曰：「臣荷恩厚，願赦李祭酒使為臣客。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen monopolized power; Li Shimin, Director of the National University, was punished with the cangue at the gate of the Imperial Academy. Zhong submitted an appended memorial saying: "I have received thick favor and wish that Director Li be pardoned to serve as my guest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Zhen held sole power, and National University director Li Shimin was shackled at the academy gate. Zhong appended a memorial: "I have received such generous favor that I ask the pardon of Director Li so he may serve as my guest.

sentences.zh: 坐無祭酒，臣不歡。」

translations.literal: Without the director present I cannot rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Without the director present I cannot be at ease.

sentences.zh: 太后立言之帝，時勉獲釋。

translations.literal: The empress dowager immediately spoke of this to the emperor, and Shimin was released.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager at once repeated this to the emperor, and Li Shimin was freed.

sentences.zh: 忠家奴貸子錢於濱州民，規利數倍，有司望風奉行，民不堪，訴諸朝，言官交章劾之。

translations.literal: A household slave of Zhong's lent money at interest to commoners in Binzhou, seeking profit several times over; officials fawned on him and enforced collection; the people could not bear it and appealed to the court; remonstrating officials submitted impeachments in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave of Zhong's lent money at usurious rates to people in Binzhou; local officials rushed to enforce the claims, the people cried out to the throne, and censorial officials impeached him in droves.

sentences.zh: 命執家奴戍邊，忠不問。

translations.literal: An order was issued to arrest the household slave and banish him to the frontier; Zhong was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The slave was seized and banished to the border; Zhong himself was not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年卒，年八十五，贈會昌侯，謚康靖。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Jingtai at age eighty-five; he was posthumously honored as Marquis of Huichang with the posthumous title Kangjing (Peaceful and Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1452 at eighty-five, and was posthumously made Marquis of Huichang with the posthumous name Peaceful and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，加贈太傅、安國公，改謚恭憲。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored the throne, he was further honored as Grand Mentor and Duke of Anguo, and his posthumous title was changed to Gongxian (Respectful and Charitable).
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong's restoration he was further honored as grand mentor and Duke of Anguo, and his posthumous name was changed to Respectful and Charitable.

sentences.zh: 成化十五年再贈太師、左柱國。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua he was again posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Left Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In 1479 he received further posthumous honors as grand preceptor and left pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 子五人：繼宗、顯宗、紹宗、續宗、純宗。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Jizong, Xianzong, Shaozong, Xuzong, and Chunzong.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Jizong, Xianzong, Shaozong, Xuzong, and Chunzong.

sentences.zh: 純宗官錦衣衛指揮僉事，早卒。

translations.literal: Chunzong held the post of Assistant Commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzong served as assistant commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and died young.

sentences.zh: 繼宗，字光輔，章皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Jizong, styled Guangfu, was elder brother to Empress Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong, styled Guangfu, was the elder brother of Empress Zhang.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，授府軍前衛指揮使，改錦衣衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande he was granted Commandership of the Forward Military Guard of the Imperial Bodyguard, then transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xuande he was made commander of the Forward Military Guard of the Imperial Bodyguard, then transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，進都指揮僉事，尋襲父爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief, and soon inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai he was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief and soon inherited his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，以奪門功，進侯，加號奉天翊衛推誠宣力武臣，特進光祿大夫、柱國，身免二死，子免一死，世襲侯爵；

translations.literal: When the Tianshun reign was proclaimed, for merit in the Gate Opening coup he was advanced to marquis, with the additional title of Grand Guardian Assisting Heaven, Supporting the Guard, and Exerting Sincere Force—Meritorious Military Subject, specially promoted Grand Master of Brilliant Blessings and Pillar of the State, with exemption from death twice for himself and once for his son, and hereditary marquis;
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianshun reign was proclaimed, for his part in the Gate-opening coup he was raised to marquis, given the fuller title of meritorious subject who supports Heaven, guards the throne, and exerts loyal force, promoted to grand master of brilliant blessings and pillar of the state, granted immunity from death twice for himself and once for his son, with a hereditary marquisate;

sentences.zh: 諸弟官都指揮僉事者，俱改錦衣衛。

translations.literal: Younger brothers who held the post of Assistant Commander-in-Chief were all transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers who had held assistant commanderships were all transferred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 復自言：「臣與弟顯宗率子、婿、家奴四十三人預奪門功，乞加恩命。」

translations.literal: He again petitioned on his own behalf: "My brother Xianzong and I, leading forty-three sons, sons-in-law, and household slaves who shared in the Gate Opening merit, beg for additional gracious appointments."
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again: "My brother Xianzong and I, with forty-three sons, sons-in-law, and household slaves who shared in the Gate-opening merit, beg additional favor.

sentences.zh: 由是顯宗進都指揮同知，子璉授錦衣衛指揮使，婿指揮使武忠進都指揮僉事，蒼頭輩授官者十七人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xianzong was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief; his son Lian was granted Commandership of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; his son-in-law, Commander Wu Zhong, was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief; and seventeen menials were granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was then promoted to vice commander-in-chief; his son Lian was made commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; his son-in-law, commander Wu Zhong, was made assistant commander-in-chief; and seventeen retainers received official posts.

sentences.zh: 五月，命督五軍營戎務兼掌後軍都督府事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was ordered to supervise military affairs of the Five Armies Camps while concurrently managing the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was ordered to supervise the military affairs of the Five Armies camps while also overseeing the rear military commission.

sentences.zh: 左右又有為紹宗求官者，帝召李賢謂曰：「孫氏一門，長封侯，次皆顯秩，子孫二十余人悉得官，足矣。

translations.literal: There were also others who pleaded on Shaozong's behalf for an office. The emperor summoned Li Xian and said: "In the Sun clan the eldest holds a marquisate while the rest hold exalted ranks; more than twenty descendants already hold office—is that not enough?
translations.idiomatic: Others soon pressed for an appointment for Shaozong. The emperor summoned Li Xian and said: "In the Sun family the eldest line holds a marquisate and the rest hold high rank; more than twenty descendants already have posts—is that not enough?

sentences.zh: 今又請以為慰太后心，不知初官其子弟時，請於太后，數請始允，且不懌者累日，曰：『何功於國，濫授此秩，物盛必衰，一旦有罪，吾不能庇矣。』

translations.literal: Now you again ask on the ground of comforting the empress dowager; yet when their kinsmen were first given office the requests went to the empress dowager, and only after several petitions did she consent—and she was displeased for days on end, saying: 'What merit have they done for the state that such ranks should be lavishly granted? When things reach their height they must decline; once guilt appears I cannot protect them.'
translations.idiomatic: You now ask again to soothe the empress dowager—but when their kin were first given posts, the requests had to go to her, and only after repeated pleading did she agree, unhappily, saying for days: 'What service have they done the state to warrant such ranks? Full measure must turn to decline; if guilt should come, I cannot shield them.'

sentences.zh: 太后意固如此。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager's mind was indeed thus."
translations.idiomatic: That was truly the empress dowager's view.

sentences.zh: 賢稽首頌太后盛德，因從容言祖宗以來，外戚不典軍政。

translations.literal: Xian kowtowed in praise of the empress dowager's great virtue, and then calmly said that since the founding emperors, affinal kin had not held military and civil command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian kowtowed in praise of her virtue, then added gently that since the dynastic founders, affinal kin had not held military command.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「初內侍言京營軍非皇舅無可屬，太后實悔至今。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At first the inner attendants said that of the capital garrison none but the empress's brother could be entrusted with it; the empress dowager has indeed regretted it to this day."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "At first the eunuchs argued that none but the empress's brother could be trusted with the capital garrison; the empress dowager has regretted it ever since.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「侯幸淳謹，但後此不得為故事耳。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "The marquis is fortunately upright and cautious, but hereafter this must not become precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian said: "The marquis is fortunately honest and careful—but this must not become precedent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 已，錦衣逯杲奏英國公張懋、太平侯張瑾及繼宗、紹宗並侵官地，立私莊。

translations.literal: Soon Su Gao of the Embroidered Uniform Guard reported that the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, the Earl of Taiping Zhang Jin, and Jizong and Shaozong alike had encroached on official lands and established private estates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Su Gao of the Embroidered Uniform Guard reported that the Duke of Ying, Zhang Mao, the Earl of Taiping, Zhang Jin, and Jizong and Shaozong alike had seized official land and set up private estates.

sentences.zh: 命各首實，懋等具服，乃宥之，典莊者悉逮問，還其地於官。

translations.literal: An order was issued for each to confess the facts; Mao and the others fully admitted guilt and were pardoned; those who managed the estates were all arrested and interrogated, and the lands were returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Each was ordered to confess fully; Mao and the others admitted their guilt and were pardoned, but the estate managers were all arrested and the land returned to the government.

sentences.zh: 石亨之獲罪也，繼宗為顯宗、武忠及子孫、家人、軍伴辭職，帝止革家人、軍伴之授職者七人，余不問。

translations.literal: When Shi Heng was punished for his crimes, Jizong submitted resignations on behalf of Xianzong, Wu Zhong, and his sons, descendants, household members, and military companions; the emperor only stripped the seven household members and military companions who had received appointments, and did not pursue the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng fell, Jizong tried to resign on behalf of Xianzong, Wu Zhong, and his sons, kin, servants, and military attendants; the emperor revoked appointments only for seven servants and attendants, and let the rest stand.

sentences.zh: 五年，曹欽平，進太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Cao Qin was suppressed, he was promoted to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after Cao Qin's rebellion was put down, he was promoted to grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾奏解兵柄，辭太保，不允。

translations.literal: Soon, citing illness, he requested release from military command and resigned the grand guardianship; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to surrender his military authority on grounds of illness and to resign as grand guardian, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，命繼宗提督十二團營兼督五軍營，知經筵事，監修《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor succeeded, Jizong was ordered to supervise the Twelve Regiments while also overseeing the Five Armies Camps, to serve in the Classics Lectures, and to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghua succeeded, Jizong was appointed to supervise the Twelve Regiments and the Five Armies camps, to attend the classics lectures, and to oversee compilation of Emperor Yingzong's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 朝有大議，必繼宗為首。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had major deliberations, Jizong invariably headed them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court debated major matters, Jizong was always listed first.

sentences.zh: 再核奪門功，惟繼宗侯如故。

translations.literal: When Gate Opening merit was reviewed again, only Jizong's marquisate remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Gate-opening honors were reexamined, only Jizong kept his marquisate unchanged.

sentences.zh: 乞休，優詔不許。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; a gracious edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire, but a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，《實錄》成，加太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, when the Veritable Records were completed, he was promoted to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, when the veritable records were finished, he was made grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 十年，兵科給事中章鎰疏言：「繼宗久司兵柄，屍位固寵，亟宜罷退，以全終始。」

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Supervising Secretary Zhang Yi of the Bureau of Military Affairs submitted a memorial saying: "Jizong has long held military power, occupying his post to secure favor; he should be removed at once to preserve a proper end."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Zhang Yi, a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, memorialized: "Jizong has held military power too long, clinging to office to keep imperial favor; he should be dismissed at once so his career may end honorably.

sentences.zh: 於是繼宗上疏懇辭，帝優詔許解營務，仍蒞後府事，知經筵，預議大政。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jizong submitted a memorial earnestly requesting release; the emperor graciously permitted him to relinquish camp duties while still attending the Rear Military Commission, serving in the Classics Lectures, and participating in major policy deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong then memorialized in earnest to resign; the emperor graciously allowed him to lay down camp duties while he continued at the rear military commission, the classics lectures, and deliberations on major state affairs.

sentences.zh: 復辭，帝不許，免其奏事承旨。

translations.literal: He again requested release; the emperor did not permit it but exempted him from presenting memorials bearing imperial commands.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again to step down; the emperor refused, but relieved him of the duty of presenting memorials on the emperor's orders.

sentences.zh: 自景泰前，戚臣無典兵者，帝見石亨、張軏輩以營軍奪門，故使外戚親臣參之，非故事也。

translations.literal: Before the Jingtai reign, no affinal kinsman had held military command; the emperor, having seen Shi Heng, Zhang Yue, and others seize the Gate through camp armies, therefore had maternal relatives and close kin participate in military affairs—not an established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Jingtai period no imperial in-law had ever commanded troops. After Shi Heng and Zhang Yue used their camp armies to force the Gate Opening, the emperor assigned affinal kin a role in military affairs—something without precedent.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒，年八十五，贈郯國公，謚榮襄。

translations.literal: Five years later he died, aged eighty-five; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Tan with the posthumous title Rongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died at eighty-five and was posthumously made Duke of Tan, posthumous name Rongxiang.

sentences.zh: 再傳至曾孫杲，詳《世表》中。

translations.literal: The line passed through two more generations to his great-grandson Gao; see the Genealogical Tables.
translations.idiomatic: After two more generations the line reached his great-grandson Gao; details appear in the Genealogical Tables.

sentences.zh: 吳安，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Wu An was a native of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu An was a native of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 父彥名，有女入侍宣宗於東宮，生景帝。

translations.literal: His father Yanming had a daughter who entered service to the Xuande Emperor in the Eastern Palace and bore the Jingdi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanming had a daughter who served in the heir apparent's palace under the Xuande Emperor and gave birth to the Jingdi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年冊為賢妃，彥名已卒，授安錦衣衛百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande she was enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort; Yanming had already died, and An was appointed centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 3 she was invested as Virtuous Consort; Yanming was already dead, and An was appointed a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，尊妃為皇太后，安進本衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor succeeded, the consort was honored as empress dowager, and An was promoted to commander of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi Emperor came to the throne, the consort was honored as empress dowager and An was promoted to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 屢遷前府左都督，弟信亦屢擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Forward Military Commission; his younger brother Xin was also repeatedly raised to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to left commissioner-in-chief of the Forward Military Commission, and his younger brother Xin was likewise promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年封安安平伯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai, An was enfeoffed as Earl of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 7 he was enfeoffed as Earl of Anping.

sentences.zh: 信早亡，官其弟敬為南京前軍左都督。

translations.literal: Xin died early; his younger brother Jing was appointed Left Commissioner-in-Chief of the Forward Army in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin died young, and his younger brother Jing was made left commissioner-in-chief of the Forward Army in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，太后復稱賢妃，降安為府軍前衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, the empress dowager was again styled Virtuous Consort, and An was demoted to vice commander of the Forward Guard of the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored, the empress dowager was again styled Virtuous Consort, and An was reduced to vice commander of the Forward Guard of the Palace Army.

sentences.zh: 敬及其群從南京錦衣衛指揮僉事智、府軍前衛指揮同知喜山、指揮僉事廣林、錦衣衛千戶誠，俱革職原籍閑住。

translations.literal: Jing, together with his clansmen—Vice Commander Zhi of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard, Assistant Commander Xishan of the Forward Guard of the Palace Army, Vice Commander Guanglin, and Centurion Cheng of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—were all stripped of office and sent to live idle in their native places.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, together with his kinsmen—Vice Commander Zhi of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard, Assistant Commander Xishan of the Forward Guard of the Palace Army, Vice Commander Guanglin, and Centurion Cheng of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—were all dismissed and sent home to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 尋命安為錦衣衛指揮使，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: Soon An was appointed commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: An was soon appointed commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, a post made hereditary for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 錢貴，海州人，英宗睿皇后父也。

translations.literal: Qian Gui was a native of Haizhou and father of Empress Xiao of Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gui was a native of Haizhou and father of Empress Xia of Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 祖整，從成祖起兵，為燕山護衛副千戶。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zheng followed the Yongle Emperor in raising troops and served as deputy centurion of the Yanshan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zheng followed the Yongle Emperor in raising troops and served as deputy centurion of the Yanshan Guard.

sentences.zh: 父通嗣職，官至金吾右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Tong inherited the post and rose to commander of the Right Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong inherited the post and eventually became commander of the Right Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 貴嗣祖職，數從成祖、宣宗北征，屢遷都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Gui inherited his grandfather's position, repeatedly followed the Yongle and Xuande emperors on northern campaigns, and was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of a guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gui inherited his grandfather's post, joined the Yongle and Xuande emperors on several northern campaigns, and was repeatedly promoted to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統七年，後將正位中宮，擢貴中府都督同知。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong, when the empress was about to take the central palace, Gui was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 7, when the empress was about to ascend the central palace, Gui was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 英宗數欲封之，後輒遜謝，故後家獨不獲封。

translations.literal: Yingzong several times wished to enfeoff him, but the empress always demurred; therefore her family alone received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong repeatedly wanted to enfeoff him, but the empress always declined on his behalf, so her family alone went without a noble title.

sentences.zh: 貴卒，長子欽為錦衣衛指揮使，與弟鐘俱歿於土木。

translations.literal: When Gui died, his eldest son Qin was commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; he and his younger brother Zhong both perished at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died, his eldest son Qin was commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; Qin and his younger brother Zhong both died at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 欽無子，以鐘遺腹子雄為後，年幼，以父錦衣故秩予優給。

translations.literal: Qin had no son; Zhong's posthumous son Xiong was made heir. While still young, he was granted preferential treatment in rank because his father had held the Embroidered Uniform Guard command.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had no son, so Zhong's posthumous son Xiong was made heir. Because the boy was young and his father had commanded the Embroidered Uniform Guard, he was granted preferential rank.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，累擢都督同知。

translations.literal: When the era changed to Tianshun, he was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianshun era began, he was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 成化時，後崩。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign the empress died.

sentences.zh: 憲宗優生母外家周氏，而薄錢氏，故後家又不獲封。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor favored the Zhou family of his birth mother's side but slighted the Qian family, so the empress's kin again received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua Emperor favored the Zhou family of his birth mother but looked coldly on the Qians, so the empress's family again received no enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 雄卒，子承宗亦屢官錦衣衛都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Xiong died, his son Chengzong also repeatedly held the post of commander-in-chief of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong died, his son Chengzong also held the post of commander-in-chief of the Embroidered Uniform Guard on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，承宗祖母王氏援憲宗外家王氏例，請封。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, Chengzong's grandmother Lady Wang, citing the precedent of the Wang family on Xianzong's maternal side, requested enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2, Chengzong's grandmother Lady Wang cited the precedent of the Wang family on Chenghua's maternal side and requested a noble title.

sentences.zh: 乃封承宗安昌伯，世襲。

translations.literal: Chengzong was then enfeoffed as Earl of Anchang, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was then enfeoffed as Earl of Anchang, with the title made hereditary.

sentences.zh: 先是，勛臣莊田租稅皆有司代收，至是王氏乞自收，始命願自收者聽，而禁管莊者橫肆。

translations.literal: Previously, rent and tax from meritorious officials' estate lands were collected by government offices; at this time Lady Wang asked to collect them herself, and an order was first issued allowing those who wished to collect for themselves to do so, while forbidding estate managers from acting outrageously.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, rent and tax from the estate lands of meritorious officials were collected by government offices. Lady Wang now asked to collect them herself, and the court first allowed anyone who wished to do so, while forbidding estate managers from acting lawlessly.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年，承宗卒，謚榮僖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing, Chengzong died and was given the posthumous title Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 5 Chengzong died and was given the posthumous title Rongxi.

sentences.zh: 子維圻嗣。

translations.literal: His son Weiji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weiji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，承宗母請以庶長子維垣嗣，詔授錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Weiji soon died; Chengzong's mother asked that the eldest son by a concubine, Weiyuan, succeed, and an edict appointed him commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji soon died; Chengzong's mother asked that the eldest son by a concubine, Weiyuan, succeed, and an edict made him commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 已又請嗣伯爵。

translations.literal: She then also asked that he inherit the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: She then also asked that he inherit the earldom.

sentences.zh: 世宗以外戚世封非祖制，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor, holding that hereditary enfeoffment of maternal kin was not ancestral institution, referred the matter to court officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor, holding that hereditary enfeoffment of maternal kin was not ancestral practice, referred the matter to the court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 八年十月上議曰：「祖宗之制，非軍功不封。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year they submitted a deliberation saying: "The institution of the ancestors was that enfeoffment was granted only for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year the court submitted its deliberation: "The ancestral rule was that enfeoffment was granted only for military merit.

sentences.zh: 洪熙時，都督張昶封彭城伯，弟升亦封惠安伯，外戚之封，自此始。

translations.literal: In the Hongxi reign, Commissioner-in-Chief Zhang Chang was enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng and his younger brother Sheng as Earl of Huian; enfeoffment of maternal kin began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongxi reign Commissioner-in-Chief Zhang Chang was enfeoffed as Earl of Pengcheng and his younger brother Sheng as Earl of Huian; enfeoffment of maternal kin began then.

sentences.zh: 循習至今，有一門數貴者，歲糜厚祿，逾分非法。

translations.literal: The practice has continued to the present; some families have several persons of high rank who each year consume rich stipends—exceeding proper bounds and contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: The practice has continued to the present, and some families now have several persons of high rank who each year consume rich stipends—an excessive and unlawful departure from proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹議：魏、定二公雖系戚裏，實佐命元勛，彭城、惠安二伯即以恩澤封，而軍功參半。

translations.literal: We respectfully deliberate: the Dukes of Wei and Ding, though maternal kin, were in fact founding supporters; the Earls of Pengcheng and Huian were enfeoffed by grace as well, with military merit accounting for half.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully propose: the Dukes of Wei and Ding, though maternal kin, were in fact founding supporters; the Earls of Pengcheng and Huian were enfeoffed by grace, yet military merit counted for half.

sentences.zh: 其余外戚恩封，毋得請襲。

translations.literal: All other grace enfeoffments of maternal kin may not be requested for inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: All other enfeoffments granted maternal kin by grace may not be requested for inheritance.

sentences.zh: 有出特恩一時寵錫者，量授指揮，千、百戶之職，終其身。」

translations.literal: Where special grace granted favor in a single instance, an appropriate appointment as commander, centurion, or platoon chief may be given for life only."
translations.idiomatic: Where special grace granted a one-time favor, an appropriate post as commander, centurion, or platoon chief may be given for life only."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The rescript said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 命魏、定、彭城、惠安襲封如故，余止終本身，著為令。

translations.literal: It ordered that inheritance of Wei, Ding, Pengcheng, and Huian continue as before; the rest would end with the person himself—established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Ding, Pengcheng, and Huian were to inherit as before; all others would hold their titles only for life. This was established as law.

sentences.zh: 維垣遂不得襲，以錦衣終。

translations.literal: Weiyuan therefore could not inherit and ended his career in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan therefore could not inherit the earldom and ended his career in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 汪泉，世為金吾左衛指揮使，家京師。

translations.literal: Wang Quan; for generations commander of the Left Jinwu Guard; family in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan's family had for generations served as commanders of the Left Jinwu Guard and lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 正統十年，其子瑛有女將冊為成阝王妃，授瑛為中城兵馬司指揮，食祿不視事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong, his son Ying had a daughter who was to be invested as imperial consort; Ying was appointed commander of the Central City Horse and Foot Command, drawing salary without attending to duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 10, Ying's daughter was chosen to enter the palace as consort; Ying was made commander of the Central City Horse and Foot Command with salary but no active duties.

sentences.zh: 妃正位中宮，進泉都指揮同知府軍衛，帶俸，瑛錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When the consort took the central palace, Quan was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Palace Army Guard with retained salary, and Ying to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort ascended the central palace, Quan was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the Palace Army Guard with retained salary, and Ying to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋並擢左都督，瑛弟亦授錦衣千戶有差。

translations.literal: Soon both were promoted to Left Commissioner-in-Chief; Ying's younger brothers were also granted centurion posts in the Embroidered Uniform Guard in varying ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Both were soon promoted to left commissioner-in-chief, and Ying's younger brothers were also given centurion posts in the Embroidered Uniform Guard in varying ranks.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，泉仍居金吾舊職，瑛錦衣舊職，其四弟皆奪官還故裏。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, Quan remained in his old Jinwu post and Ying in his old Embroidered Uniform Guard post; the four younger brothers were all stripped of office and returned to their native region.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored, Quan kept his old Jinwu post and Ying his old Embroidered Uniform Guard post, but the four younger brothers were stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋命瑛錦衣指揮僉事，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: Soon Ying was appointed vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, hereditary for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was soon appointed vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, a post made hereditary for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 杭昱，女為景帝妃，生子見濟。

translations.literal: Hang Yu; his daughter was consort of the Jingdi Emperor and bore Zhanji.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yu's daughter was consort to the Jingdi Emperor and bore Zhanji.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，帝欲廢英宗子而立己子，乃廢皇后汪氏，冊妃為后。
