translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, the emperor wished to set aside Yingzong's son and establish his own, so he deposed Empress Wang and enfeoffed the consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3 the emperor wished to set aside Yingzong's son and establish his own, so he deposed Empress Wang and invested the consort as empress.

sentences.zh: 昱累官錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Yu repeatedly held the post of commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose repeatedly to commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 兄聚授錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ju was appointed centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ju was appointed a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 聚尋卒，賜賻及祭葬。

translations.literal: Ju soon died and was granted funeral subsidies and sacrificial burial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ju soon died and was granted funeral subsidies and sacrificial burial honors.

sentences.zh: 七年，後崩，官其弟敏錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the empress died; his younger brother Min was appointed centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the empress died, and his younger brother Min was appointed a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，盡奪景帝所授外親官，尤惡杭氏，昱已前卒，敏削職還裏。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, he stripped all maternal kin of offices granted by the Jingdi Emperor, especially hated the Hang clan; Yu had already died earlier, and Min was stripped of office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored, he stripped all maternal kin of the offices Jingdi had granted them and especially hated the Hangs; Yu had already died, and Min was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 周能，字廷舉，昌平人。

translations.literal: Zhou Neng, styled Tingju, a native of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Neng, styled Tingju, was a native of Changping.

sentences.zh: 女為英宗妃，生憲宗，是為孝肅皇太后。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort of Yingzong and bore the Xianzong Emperor—who is known as Empress Dowager Xiaosu.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was consort to Yingzong and bore the Chenghua Emperor, who is known as Empress Dowager Xiaosu.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，授能錦衣衛千戶，賜賫甚渥。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, Neng was appointed centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and granted exceptionally generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was restored, Neng was appointed a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and given exceptionally generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 能卒，長子壽嗣職。

translations.literal: When Neng died, his eldest son Shou inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Neng died, his eldest son Shou inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 憲宗踐阼，擢左府都督同知。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Shou was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Left Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghua ascended the throne, Shou was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Left Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 成化三年封慶雲伯，贈能慶雲侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua he was enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyun, and Neng was posthumously made Marquis of Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 3 he was enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyun, and Neng was posthumously made Marquis of Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 壽以太后弟，頗恣橫。

translations.literal: As the empress dowager's younger brother, Shou was rather overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress dowager's younger brother, Shou was quite overbearing.

sentences.zh: 時方禁勛戚請乞莊田，壽獨冒禁乞通州田六十二頃，不得已與之。

translations.literal: At the time meritorious officials and imperial kin were forbidden to request estate lands; Shou alone defied the ban and asked for sixty-two qing of land in Tongzhou, and it was granted against the court's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time meritorious officials and imperial kin were forbidden to request estate lands, but Shou alone defied the ban and asked for sixty-two qing in Tongzhou, and the court reluctantly granted it.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使，道呂梁洪，多挾商艘。

translations.literal: Once on an official mission he passed Lüliang Rapid and took many merchant vessels in tow.
translations.idiomatic: Once while on official business he passed Lüliang Rapid and requisitioned many merchant vessels.

sentences.zh: 主事謝敬不可，壽與哄，且劾之，敬坐落陽。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Xie Jing refused; Shou quarreled with him and also impeached him, and Jing was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Xie Jing objected; Shou brawled with him and impeached him, and Jing lost his post.

sentences.zh: 十七年進侯，子弟同日授錦衣官者七人，能追贈太傅、寧國公，謚榮靖。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to marquis; seven sons and nephews received Embroidered Uniform Guard posts on the same day; Neng was posthumously made Grand Mentor and Duke of Ning, posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to marquis; seven sons and nephews received Embroidered Uniform Guard posts on the same day; Neng was posthumously made grand mentor and Duke of Ning, posthumous name Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，壽加太保。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended, Shou was made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi Emperor came to the throne, Shou was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 時壽所賜莊田甚多，其在寶坻者已五百頃，又欲得其余七百余頃，詭言以私財相易。

translations.literal: By then Shou had been granted many estate lands; he already held five hundred qing in Baodi and wished to obtain another seven hundred-odd qing, falsely claiming he would exchange private property for them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shou had been granted many estate lands; he already held five hundred qing in Baodi and wanted another seven hundred-odd qing, falsely claiming he would exchange private property for them.

sentences.zh: 部劾其貪求無厭，執不許，孝宗竟許之。

translations.literal: The ministry impeached his insatiable greed and steadfastly refused; Xiaozong nevertheless approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry impeached his insatiable greed and refused, but the Hongzhi Emperor approved the request anyway.

sentences.zh: 又與建昌侯張延齡爭田，兩家奴相毆，交章上聞。

translations.literal: He also disputed land with Marquis Jianchang Zhang Yanling; the two households' servants fought each other, and memorials from both sides reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also disputed land with Marquis Jianchang Zhang Yanling; servants of both households fought, and memorials from both sides reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 又數撓鹽法，侵公家利，有司厭苦之。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly meddled with the salt monopoly, encroaching on public revenue, to the exasperation of local officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly meddled with the salt monopoly and encroached on public revenue, to the exasperation of local officials.

sentences.zh: 十六年加太傅，弟長寧伯彧亦加太保，兄弟並為侯伯，位三公，前此未有也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made Grand Mentor; his younger brother Yu, Earl of Changning, was also made Grand Guardian—the brothers both held marquis or earl rank and the Three Excellencies, unprecedented before this.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand mentor, and his younger brother Yu, Earl of Changning, was also made grand guardian—the brothers both held marquis or earl rank and the Three Excellencies, something without precedent.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，汰傳奉官，壽子侄八人在汰中，壽上章乞留，從之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended, supernumerary appointees were purged; eight of Shou's sons and nephews were among those cut; Shou memorialized asking they be retained, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor came to the throne, supernumerary appointees were purged; eight of Shou's sons and nephews were among those cut, but Shou memorialized asking that they be retained, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 正德四年卒，贈宣國公，謚恭和。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he died and was posthumously made Duke of Xuan, posthumous title Gonghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4 he died and was posthumously made Duke of Xuan, posthumous name Gonghe.

sentences.zh: 子瑛嗣，封殖過於父。

translations.literal: His son Ying succeeded and accumulated estates beyond what his father had.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying succeeded him and amassed estates even beyond what his father had.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，於河西務設肆邀商貨，虐市民，虧國課，為巡按御史所劾，停祿三月。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he set up shops at Hexiwu to intercept merchants' goods, abused townsmen, and reduced state revenue; a touring censor impeached him and his salary was suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he set up shops at Hexiwu to intercept merchants' goods, abused townspeople, and reduced state revenue; a touring censor impeached him and his salary was suspended for three months.

sentences.zh: 而瑛怙惡如故，又為主事翁萬達所劾，詔革其廛肆，下家人於法司。

translations.literal: Yet Ying persisted in his wickedness; Chief Clerk Weng Wanda impeached him again, and an edict abolished his shops and handed his household retainers over to the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ying persisted in his wickedness; chief clerk Weng Wanda impeached him again, and an edict abolished his shops and handed his household retainers over to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 時已革外戚世爵，瑛卒，遂不得嗣。

translations.literal: By then hereditary noble titles for maternal kin had been abolished; when Ying died he could not pass on the title.
translations.idiomatic: By then hereditary noble titles for maternal kin had been abolished, and when Ying died he could not pass on the title.

sentences.zh: 彧，太后仲弟也。

translations.literal: Yu was the empress dowager's second younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the empress dowager's second younger brother.

sentences.zh: 成化時，累官左府都督同知。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign he repeatedly held the post of vice commissioner-in-chief of the Left Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he repeatedly held the post of vice commissioner-in-chief of the Left Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十一年封長寧伯，世襲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Changning, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Changning, with the title made hereditary.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，外戚經營私利，彧與壽寧侯張鶴齡至聚眾相鬥，都下震駭。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, as maternal kin pursued private profit, Yu and Zhang Heling, Marquis of Shouning, even gathered crowds to fight each other, shocking the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, as maternal kin pursued private profit, Yu and Zhang Heling, Marquis of Shouning, even gathered crowds to fight each other, shocking the capital.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，尚書屠滽偕九卿上言：

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year, Minister Tu Yong together with the Nine Ministers submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year, Minister Tu Yong together with the Nine Ministers submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 憲宗皇帝詔，勛戚之家，不得占據關津陂澤，設肆開廛，侵奪民利，違者許所在官司執治以聞。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor decreed that meritorious officials' and imperial kin's households must not occupy passes, fords, ponds, and marshes, establish shops and open market stalls, or seize the people's profit; violators were to be arrested by local offices and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua Emperor decreed that the households of meritorious officials and imperial kin must not occupy passes, fords, ponds, and marshes, establish shops and open market stalls, or seize the people's profit; violators were to be arrested by local offices and reported.

sentences.zh: 皇上踐極，亦惟先帝之法是訓是遵。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, you likewise took the former emperor's laws as your instruction and guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, you likewise took the former emperor's laws as your instruction and guide.

sentences.zh: 而勛戚諸臣不能恪守先詔，縱家人列肆通衢，邀截商貨，都城內外，所在有之。

translations.literal: Yet meritorious officials and imperial kin have not faithfully kept the former decree, letting household members set up stalls along thoroughfares and intercept merchants' goods—inside and outside the capital, this occurs everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet meritorious officials and imperial kin have not faithfully kept the former decree, letting household members set up stalls along thoroughfares and intercept merchants' goods—inside and outside the capital, this occurs everywhere.

sentences.zh: 觀永樂間榜例，王公仆從二十人，一品不過十二人。

translations.literal: Consider the Yongle-era posted regulations: princes and dukes were limited to twenty servants; first-rank officials to no more than twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Yongle-era posted regulations: princes and dukes were limited to twenty servants, and first-rank officials to no more than twelve.

sentences.zh: 今勛戚多者以百數，大乖舊制。

translations.literal: Today some meritorious officials and imperial kin have household members numbering in the hundreds—a great departure from the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Today some meritorious officials and imperial kin have household members numbering in the hundreds—a great departure from the old system.

sentences.zh: 其間多市井無賴，冒名罔利，利歸群小，怨叢一身，非計之得。

translations.literal: Many among them are market riffraff who borrow names to seek profit; gain goes to the mob while resentment gathers on one man—not a winning strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Many among them are market riffraff who borrow names to seek profit; gain goes to the mob while resentment gathers on one man—not a winning strategy.

sentences.zh: 邇者長寧伯周彧、壽寧侯張鶴齡兩家，以瑣事忿爭，喧傳都邑，失戚裏之觀瞻，損朝廷之威重。

translations.literal: Recently the households of Earl of Changning Zhou Yu and Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling quarreled over a trivial matter; the uproar spread through the capital, unbecoming to imperial in-laws and diminishing the court's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the households of Earl of Changning Zhou Yu and Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling quarreled over a trivial matter; the uproar spread through the capital, unbecoming to imperial in-laws and diminishing the court's dignity.

sentences.zh: 伏望綸音戒諭，俾各修舊好。

translations.literal: We humbly hope for an imperial edict of admonition so each may restore former goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hope for an imperial edict of admonition so each may restore former goodwill.

sentences.zh: 凡在店肆，悉皆停止。

translations.literal: All shop stalls should be closed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: All shop stalls should be closed entirely.

sentences.zh: 更敕都察院揭榜禁戒，擾商賈、奪民利者，聽巡城巡按御史及所在有司執治。

translations.literal: Further command the Censorate to post prohibitions: those who harass merchants or seize the people's profit may be arrested by city-patrol and touring censors and local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Further command the Censorate to post prohibitions: those who harass merchants or seize the people's profit may be arrested by city-patrol and touring censors and local officials.

sentences.zh: 仍考永樂間榜例，裁定勛戚家人，不得濫收。

translations.literal: Still examine the Yongle posted regulations and fix limits on meritorious officials' and imperial kin's household members—they must not be taken on indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Still examine the Yongle posted regulations and fix limits on the household members of meritorious officials and imperial kin—they must not be taken on indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 科道亦以為言，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The censorial and remonstrance officials also spoke on the matter, and the emperor praised and accepted their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial and remonstrance officials also spoke on the matter, and the emperor praised and accepted their advice.

sentences.zh: 十八年進太保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 彧求為侯，吏部言封爵出自朝廷，無請乞者，乃止。

translations.literal: Yu asked to be made marquis; the Ministry of Personnel said enfeoffment comes from the court and there is no one who requests it—so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked to be made marquis; the Ministry of Personnel said enfeoffment comes from the court and no one should request it, so he desisted.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，悉擢彧子瑭等六人為錦衣官。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended, all six of Yu's sons including Tao were promoted to Embroidered Uniform Guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor came to the throne, all six of Yu's sons including Tao were promoted to Embroidered Uniform Guard posts.

sentences.zh: 彧尋卒。

translations.literal: Yu soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu soon died.

sentences.zh: 傳子瑭，孫大經，及曾孫世臣，降授錦衣衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: In succession his son Tang, grandson Dajing, and great-grandson Shichen were demoted and granted the post of vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In turn his son Tang, his grandson Dajing, and his great-grandson Shichen were demoted to vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，孝肅有弟吉祥，兒時出遊，去為僧，家人莫知所在，孝肅亦若忘之。

translations.literal: Previously, Empress Xiaosu had a younger brother Jixiang who went out to play as a child, left and became a monk; the family did not know where he was, and Xiaosu too seemed to have forgotten him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Xiaosu had had a younger brother named Jixiang who vanished in childhood while out playing and became a monk; the family lost track of him, and even Xiaosu seemed to have forgotten him.

sentences.zh: 一夕，夢伽藍神來，言後弟今在某所，英宗亦同時夢。

translations.literal: One night she dreamed the monastery guardian deity came and said her younger brother was now at a certain place; the Yingzong Emperor also dreamed the same dream at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: One night she dreamed that the guardian deity of a monastery came and said her brother was now at a certain place—and the Yingzong Emperor had the same dream at the same time.

sentences.zh: 旦遣小黃門，以夢中言物色，得之報國寺伽藍殿中，召入見。

translations.literal: At dawn she sent a eunuch attendant to search according to the dream's words; he was found in the guardian hall of Baoguo Monastery and summoned in for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn she sent a eunuch attendant to search as the dream directed; he was found in the guardian hall of Baoguo Monastery and brought in to see her.

sentences.zh: 後且喜且泣，欲爵之不可，厚賜遣還。

translations.literal: The empress was by turns joyful and tearful; she wished to ennoble him but could not, gave him rich gifts, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept and rejoiced by turns; she wanted to ennoble him but could not, and instead gave him rich gifts and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，為建大慈仁寺，賜莊田數百頃。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor ascended, he built the Great Ciren Monastery for him and granted several hundred qing of estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua Emperor came to the throne, he built the Great Ciren Monastery for Jixiang and granted it several hundred qing of estate lands.

sentences.zh: 其後，周氏衰落，而慈仁寺莊田久猶存。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Zhou clan declined, yet the Ciren Monastery's estate lands long remained.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Zhou clan fell from power, but the Ciren Monastery's estate lands endured for a long time.

sentences.zh: 王鎮，字克安，上元人，憲宗純皇后父也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, styled Ke'an, a native of Shangyuan, was the father of the Xianzong Emperor's Empress Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, styled Ke'an, was a native of Shangyuan and father of Empress Chun, consort of the Chenghua Emperor.

sentences.zh: 成化初，授金吾左衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was appointed commander of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chenghua reign he was appointed commander of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，後將正位中宮，拜中軍都督同知。

translations.literal: Before long, as the empress was about to take her place in the inner palace, he was appointed vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as his daughter was about to become empress, he was made vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 四年進右都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 鎮為人厚重清謹，雖榮寵，不改其素，有長者稱。

translations.literal: Zhen was by nature weighty, dignified, and pure in his caution; though honored and favored, he did not change his plain ways, and was known as a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was sober, dignified, and scrupulous; though showered with honors, he did not change his plain habits, and was known as a man of worth.

sentences.zh: 十年六月卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年追封阜國公，謚康穆。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Fuguo, with the posthumous title Kangmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Fuguo, with the posthumous title Kangmu, "Peaceful and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 子三人：源，清，浚。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yuan, Qing, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yuan, Qing, and Jun.

sentences.zh: 源，字宗本，後弟也。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Zongben, was the empress's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Zongben, was the empress's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 父卒，授錦衣衛都指揮使。

translations.literal: When his father died, he was appointed chief commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was appointed chief commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 外戚例有賜田，源家奴怙勢，多侵靜海縣民業。

translations.literal: Maternal kin customarily received granted lands; Yuan's household slaves relied on his power and encroached heavily on the common people's holdings in Jinghai County.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial in-laws were routinely granted lands, but Yuan's household slaves, trading on his influence, seized large tracts of commoners' property in Jinghai County.

sentences.zh: 十六年，給事中王垣等言：「永樂、宣德間，許畿輔八郡民盡力墾荒，永免其稅，所以培國本重王畿也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Secretariat Receivers Wang Yuan and others said: "During Yongle and Xuande, the people of the eight metropolitan districts were permitted to reclaim wasteland with all their strength and granted permanent tax exemption—the purpose being to nurture the state's foundation and honor the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Secretariat Receivers Wang Yuan and others said: "Under Yongle and Xuande, the people of the eight metropolitan districts were allowed to reclaim wasteland with all their strength and granted permanent tax exemption—meant to strengthen the state's foundation and honor the capital region.

sentences.zh: 外戚王源賜田，初止二十七頃，乃令其家奴別立四至，占奪民產至二千二百余頃。

translations.literal: The maternal kinsman Wang Yuan's granted land initially amounted to only twenty-seven qing, yet he had his household slaves set new boundaries and seize commoners' property totaling more than twenty-two hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kinsman Wang Yuan had originally been granted only twenty-seven qing, yet his household slaves marked out new boundaries and seized more than twenty-two hundred qing of commoners' land.

sentences.zh: 及貧民赴告，御史劉喬徇情曲奏，致源無忌憚，家奴益橫。

translations.literal: When the poor brought complaints, Censor Liu Qiao bent the report out of partiality, leaving Yuan without restraint, and the household slaves grew ever more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When the poor petitioned for redress, Censor Liu Qiao filed a biased report, leaving Yuan unchecked and his household slaves ever more brazen.

sentences.zh: 今戶部郎中張禎叔等再按得實，乞自原額外悉還氏，並治喬罪。」

translations.literal: Now Ministry of Revenue Director Zhang Zhishu and others have reinvestigated and found the facts; we beg that everything beyond the original allotment be fully returned to the people, and that Qiao be punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ministry of Revenue Director Zhang Zhishu and others have reinvestigated and confirmed the facts; we ask that everything beyond the original grant be returned to the people, and that Qiao be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and sharply rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 後詔禁外戚侵民產，源悉歸所占於民，人多其能改過。

translations.literal: Later an edict forbade maternal kin from encroaching on commoners' property; Yuan fully returned what had been seized, and many praised his ability to mend his ways.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict forbade imperial in-laws from seizing commoners' property; Yuan returned everything he had taken, and many praised his willingness to reform.

sentences.zh: 十八年擢中軍都督同知。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十年封瑞安伯。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ruian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ruian.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 十六年加太保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 武宗登極，進太傅，增祿至七百石。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to grand tutor and his stipend was raised to seven hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor came to the throne, he was promoted to grand tutor and his stipend was raised to seven hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年卒，贈太師，謚榮靖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he died; he was posthumously made grand preceptor with the posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jiajing and was posthumously made grand preceptor, with the posthumous title Rongjing, "Glorious and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 清，成化十八年授錦衣衛千戶，累官中軍都督同知。

translations.literal: Qing, in the eighteenth year of Chenghua was appointed battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and rose through posts to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was appointed a battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard in the eighteenth year of Chenghua and rose through the ranks to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年封崇善伯。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi he was enfeoffed as Earl of Chongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Hongzhi he was enfeoffed as Earl of Chongshan.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，加太保。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was made grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 浚，成化十八年授錦衣衛百戶。

translations.literal: Jun, in the eighteenth year of Chenghua was appointed company commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was appointed a company commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard in the eighteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 兄清每遷職，輒以浚代，歷官中軍左都督。

translations.literal: Each time his elder brother Qing was promoted, Jun replaced him in his former post; he rose through ranks to left commander-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Each time his elder brother Qing was promoted, Jun stepped into the post he vacated, eventually rising to left commander-in-chief of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 正德二年封安仁伯，逾月卒，贈侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was enfeoffed as Earl of Anren; a month later he died and was posthumously granted the rank of marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was enfeoffed as Earl of Anren; a month later he died and was posthumously raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 浚兄弟三人並貴顯，皆謙慎守禮，在戚里中以賢稱。

translations.literal: Jun and his two brothers all rose to eminence, yet each was modest, cautious, and observant of propriety, and among imperial in-laws they were known for worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and his two brothers all rose to eminence, yet each remained modest and scrupulous in propriety, and among imperial in-laws they were known for their virtue.

sentences.zh: 源子橋、浚子桓，皆嗣伯。

translations.literal: Yuan's son Qiao and Jun's son Huan each inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's son Qiao and Jun's son Huan each inherited their fathers' earldoms.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中並清子極皆以例降革。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era Qing's son Ji and the others were all reduced and stripped of rank according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era Qing's son Ji and the others were all demoted and stripped of rank under the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 萬貴，憲宗萬貴妃父也，歷官錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Wan Gui was the father of the Xianzong Emperor's Consort Wan; he held the post of commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Gui, father of Consort Wan of the Chenghua Emperor, served as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 貴頗謹飭，每受賜，輒憂形於色曰：「吾起掾史，編尺伍，蒙天子恩，備戚屬，子姓皆得官。

translations.literal: Gui was quite strict and disciplined; each time he received an imperial gift, worry showed on his face as he said: "I rose from clerk and army rolls, received the Son of Heaven's grace, became an imperial kinsman, and all my descendants have gained office.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was a disciplined man; whenever he received an imperial gift, worry showed on his face. "I rose from clerk and army rolls," he would say, "received the Son of Heaven's grace, became an imperial kinsman, and all my descendants have gained office.

sentences.zh: 福過災生，未知所終矣。」

translations.literal: When blessing exceeds measure, disaster is born—I do not know how this will end.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune runs too high, disaster follows—I do not know how this will end.

sentences.zh: 時貴妃方擅寵，貴子喜為指揮使，與弟通、達等並驕橫。

translations.literal: At that time the consort was monopolizing favor; Gui's son Xi served as commander, and together with his brothers Tong and Da they were all arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort Wan held the emperor's exclusive favor; Gui's son Xi served as commander, and he and his brothers Tong and Da were all arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 貴每見諸子屑越賜物，輒戒曰：「官所賜，皆著籍。

translations.literal: Whenever Gui saw his sons treat imperial gifts lightly, he would warn them: "What the court grants is all entered in the register.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gui saw his sons treat imperial gifts casually, he would warn them: "Everything the court grants is entered in the register.

sentences.zh: 他日復宣索，汝曹將重得罪。」

translations.literal: One day if the edict comes again to demand return, you will commit grave offense.
translations.idiomatic: If the court one day sends an edict demanding them back, you will commit a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 諸子笑以為迂。

translations.literal: His sons laughed, thinking him obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: His sons laughed and dismissed him as old-fashioned.

sentences.zh: 成化十年卒，賻贈祭葬有加。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua he died; funerary gifts, posthumous honors, and sacrificial rites were all augmented.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Chenghua; the court granted augmented funerary gifts, posthumous honors, and sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 十四年進喜都指揮同知，通指揮使，達指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Xi was promoted to vice chief commander, Tong to commander, and Da to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Xi was promoted to vice chief commander, Tong to commander, and Da to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 通少貧賤，業賈。

translations.literal: Tong had been poor and lowly in youth and traded for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had been poor and lowly in youth and made his living as a merchant.

sentences.zh: 既驟貴，益貪黷無厭，造奇巧邀利。

translations.literal: Once suddenly elevated, he grew ever more greedy and corrupt without limit, devising ingenious contrivances to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: Once suddenly elevated, he grew ever greedier and more corrupt, devising ingenious schemes to turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 中官韋興、梁芳等復為左右，每進一物，輒出內庫償，輦金錢絡繹不絕。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Wei Xing, Liang Fang, and others again served as his backers; for each item presented the inner treasury paid compensation, and carts of gold and cash flowed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Wei Xing, Liang Fang, and others again backed him; for every item he presented the inner treasury paid compensation, and carts of gold and cash flowed without end.

sentences.zh: 通妻王出入宮掖，大學士萬安附通為同宗，婢仆朝夕至王所，謁起居。

translations.literal: Tong's wife Wang went in and out of the palace women's quarters; Grand Secretary Wan An attached himself to Tong as a fellow clansman, and maids and servants came morning and evening to Wang's residence to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's wife Wang moved freely in and out of the palace women's quarters; Grand Secretary Wan An claimed kinship with Tong, and maids and servants came morning and evening to Wang's residence to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 妖人李孜省輩皆緣喜進，朝野苦之。

translations.literal: Sorcerers such as Li Zisheng all advanced through Xi; court and countryside suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerers such as Li Zisheng all rose through Xi's patronage, to the distress of court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 通死，帝眷萬氏不已，遷喜都督同知，達指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Tong died, the emperor's affection for the Wan clan did not cease; Xi was transferred to vice commissioner-in-chief and Da to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong died, the emperor's favor toward the Wan clan did not wane; Xi was made vice commissioner-in-chief and Da vice commander.

sentences.zh: 通庶子方二歲，養子方四歲，俱授官。

translations.literal: Tong's sons by a concubine, aged barely two, and an adopted son, aged barely four, were both granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's two-year-old son by a concubine and his four-year-old adopted son were both granted offices.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghua Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 言官劾其罪狀。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials impeached their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials impeached them for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乃奪喜等官，而盡追封誥及內帑賜物，如貴言。

translations.literal: The Xiaozong Emperor then stripped Xi and the others of their offices and fully recovered enfeoffment patents, edicts, and inner-treasury gifts—just as Gui had foretold.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi Emperor then stripped Xi and the others of their offices and recovered all patents of enfeoffment, edicts, and gifts from the inner treasury—just as Gui had warned.

sentences.zh: 邵喜，昌化人，世宗大母邵太后弟也。

translations.literal: Shao Xi, a native of Changhua, was the younger brother of the Jiajing Emperor's grandmother, Empress Dowager Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xi, a native of Changhua, was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Shao, grandmother of the Jiajing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，封喜昌化伯，明年卒。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended, Xi was enfeoffed as Earl of Changhua; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, Xi was enfeoffed as Earl of Changhua; he died the following year.

sentences.zh: 子蕙嗣，嘉靖六年卒，無子，族人爭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hui succeeded; in the sixth year of Jiajing he died without a son, and clansmen disputed the succession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui succeeded him; Hui died in the sixth year of Jiajing without an heir, and clansmen fought over the succession.

sentences.zh: 初，太后入宮時，父林早歿。

translations.literal: At first, when the empress dowager entered the palace, her father Lin had already died early.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager first entered the palace, her father Lin had already died.

sentences.zh: 太后弟四人：宗、安、宣、喜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had four younger brothers: Zong, An, Xuan, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had four younger brothers: Zong, An, Xuan, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 宗、宣無後，及蕙卒，帝令蕙弟萱嗣。

translations.literal: Zong and Xuan had no heirs; when Hui died, the emperor ordered Hui's younger brother Xuan to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zong and Xuan left no heirs; when Hui died, the emperor ordered Hui's younger brother Xuan to succeed.

sentences.zh: 蕙侄錦衣指揮輔、千戶茂言，萱非嫡派，不當襲，蕙母爭之，議久不決。

translations.literal: Hui's nephew, Guard Commander Fu and Battalion Commander Mao Yan, argued that Xuan was not of the direct line and should not inherit; Hui's mother contested this, and deliberation dragged on unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's nephews, Guard Commander Fu and Battalion Commander Mao Yan, argued that Xuan was not of the direct line and should not inherit; Hui's mother contested the point, and the dispute dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 大學士張璁等言：「邵氏子孫已絕，今其爭者皆旁枝，不宜嗣。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and others said: "The Shao clan's descendants are extinct; those disputing now are all collateral branches and ought not to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and others said: "The Shao line is extinct; those disputing the succession are all collateral branches and ought not to inherit.

sentences.zh: 時帝必欲為喜立後，乃以喜兄安之孫傑為昌化伯。

translations.literal: The emperor was determined to establish an heir for Xi, so he made Jie, grandson of Xi's elder brother An, Earl of Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was determined to establish an heir for Xi, so he made Jie, grandson of Xi's elder brother An, Earl of Changhua.

sentences.zh: 明年，《明倫大典》成，命武定侯郭勛頒賜戚畹，弗及傑。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Great Compendium of Human Relations was completed, the emperor ordered Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun to distribute copies to imperial kin—Jie was not included.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Great Compendium of Human Relations was completed, the emperor ordered Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun to distribute copies among imperial in-laws—but Jie was not included.

sentences.zh: 傑自請之，帝詰勛。

translations.literal: Jie requested a copy himself; the emperor questioned Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jie asked for a copy himself, and the emperor questioned Xun.

sentences.zh: 勛怒，錄邵氏爭襲章奏，訐傑實他姓，請覆勘，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Xun grew angry, compiled the Shao clan's succession dispute memorials, denounced Jie as actually of another surname, and asked for reinvestigation; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xun grew angry, assembled the Shao succession dispute memorials, accused Jie of being of another surname altogether, and asked for reinvestigation; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 會給事中陸粲論大學士桂萼受傑賂，使奴隸冒封爵。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Secretariat Receiver Lu Can accused Grand Secretary Gui E of accepting bribes from Jie and using a slave to fraudulently obtain enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Secretariat Receiver Lu Can accused Grand Secretary Gui E of taking bribes from Jie and using a slave to obtain enfeoffment by fraud.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下粲獄，而盡革外戚封，傑亦奪襲。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, imprisoned Can, and stripped all maternal kin of their enfeoffments; Jie too lost his succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, imprisoned Can, and stripped all imperial in-laws of their enfeoffments; Jie too lost his title.

sentences.zh: 張巒，敬皇后父也。

translations.literal: Zhang Luan was the father of Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Luan was the father of Empress Jing.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年封壽寧伯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shouning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shouning.

sentences.zh: 立皇太子，進為侯。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was established, he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was established, he was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒贈昌國公，子鶴齡嗣侯。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted Duke of Changguo; his son Heling succeeded to the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Duke of Changguo; his son Heling inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 十六年，其弟延齡亦由建昌伯進爵侯。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year his younger brother Yanling was also advanced from Earl of Jianchang to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his younger brother Yanling was also raised from Earl of Jianchang to marquis.

sentences.zh: 巒起諸生，雖貴盛，能敬禮士大夫。

translations.literal: Luan had risen from a common licentiate; though greatly honored, he could show respect to scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Luan had risen from the ranks of licentiates; though greatly honored, he treated scholar-officials with respect.

sentences.zh: 鶴齡兄弟並驕肆，縱家奴奪民田廬，篡獄囚，數犯法。

translations.literal: Heling and his brothers were together arrogant and unrestrained, letting household slaves seize commoners' fields and dwellings, rescuing prisoners from jail, and repeatedly breaking the law.
translations.idiomatic: Heling and his brothers were arrogant and unrestrained, letting household slaves seize commoners' fields and homes, springing prisoners from jail, and repeatedly breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 帝遣侍郎屠勛、太監蕭敬按得實，坐奴如律。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Vice Minister Tu Xun and eunuch Xiao Jing to investigate; they found the facts and punished the slaves according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Tu Xun and the eunuch Xiao Jing to investigate; they confirmed the facts and punished the slaves according to law.

sentences.zh: 敬復命，皇后怒，帝亦佯怒。

translations.literal: When Jing reported back, the empress was angry, and the emperor feigned anger as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing reported back, the empress was furious, and the emperor feigned anger as well.

sentences.zh: 已而召敬曰：「汝言是也。」

translations.literal: Soon after he summoned Jing and said: "What you said is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he summoned Jing and said, "What you reported is correct.

sentences.zh: 賜之金。

translations.literal: He was given gold.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with gold.

sentences.zh: 給事中吳世忠、主事李夢陽皆以劾延齡幾得罪。

translations.literal: Secretariat Receivers Wu Shizhong and Section Chief Li Mengyang both nearly suffered punishment for impeaching Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Receivers Wu Shizhong and Section Chief Li Mengyang both nearly came to grief for impeaching Yanling.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝遊南宮，鶴齡兄弟入侍。

translations.literal: On another day the emperor visited the Southern Palace, and the Heling brothers attended him.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor visited the Southern Palace, and the Heling brothers attended him.

sentences.zh: 酒半，皇后、皇太子及鶴齡母金夫人起更衣，因出遊覽。

translations.literal: When the wine was half finished, the empress, crown prince, and Heling's mother Lady Jin rose to change clothes and went out sight-seeing.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was half finished, the empress, the crown prince, and Heling's mother Lady Jin withdrew to change clothes and went out sight-seeing.

sentences.zh: 帝獨召鶴齡語，左右莫得聞，遙見鶴齡免冠首觸地，自是稍斂跡。

translations.literal: The emperor alone summoned Heling to speak; attendants could not hear, but from afar they saw Heling bare his head and knock it on the ground; from then on he somewhat restrained his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Heling alone to speak; attendants could not hear what was said, but from a distance they saw Heling bare his head and knock it on the ground; from then on he somewhat checked his behavior.

sentences.zh: 正德中，鶴齡進太傅。

translations.literal: During Zhengde he was promoted to grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was promoted to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 世宗入繼，鶴齡以定策功，進封昌國公。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor succeeded, Heling was advanced to Duke of Changguo for his merit in settling the succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor succeeded to the throne, Heling was raised to Duke of Changguo for his role in settling the succession.

sentences.zh: 時敬皇后已改稱皇伯母昭聖皇太后矣。

translations.literal: By then Empress Jing had already been restyled Grand Imperial Aunt, Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: By then Empress Jing had already been restyled Grand Imperial Aunt, Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 帝以太后抑其母蔣太后故，銜張氏。

translations.literal: Because the empress dowager had suppressed his mother, Empress Dowager Jiang, the emperor harbored resentment toward the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empress dowager had slighted his mother, Empress Dowager Jiang, the emperor bore a grudge against the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十二年，延齡有罪下獄，坐死，並革鶴齡爵，謫南京錦衣衛指揮同知，太后為請不得。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiajing Yanling was guilty, imprisoned, and sentenced to death; Heling's title was also stripped and he was demoted to vice commander of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard—the empress dowager pleaded for him in vain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jiajing Yanling was imprisoned on criminal charges and sentenced to death; Heling's title was also stripped and he was demoted to vice commander of the Nanjing Embroidered Uniform Guard—the empress dowager pleaded for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 初，正德時，日者曹祖告其子鼎為延齡奴，與延齡謀不軌。

translations.literal: At first, during Zhengde, the diviner Cao Zu reported that his son Ding was Yanling's slave and had plotted treason with Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhengde reign, the diviner Cao Zu reported that his son Ding was Yanling's servant and had plotted treason with him.

sentences.zh: 武宗下之獄，將集群臣廷鞫之，祖仰藥死。

translations.literal: The Wuzong Emperor imprisoned them and was about to convene the ministers for a court interrogation when Zu swallowed poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde Emperor had them imprisoned and was about to convene the ministers for a court interrogation when Zu swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: 時頗以祖暴死疑延齡，而獄無左證，遂解。

translations.literal: At the time many suspected Yanling because of Zu's sudden death, but the case lacked corroborating evidence and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Many then suspected Yanling because of Zu's sudden death, but the case lacked corroborating evidence and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 指揮司聰者，為延齡行錢，負其五百金。

translations.literal: A commander named Si Cong had handled money for Yanling and owed him five hundred ounces of gold.
translations.idiomatic: A commander named Si Cong had handled money for Yanling and owed him five hundred ounces of gold.

sentences.zh: 索之急，遂與天文生董昶子至謀訐祖前所首事，脅延齡賄。

translations.literal: When Yanling pressed him urgently for payment, Cong joined with the astronomer Dong Chang's son Zhi in plotting to denounce the affair Zu had previously reported, extorting a bribe from Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling pressed him hard for payment, Cong joined with the astronomer Dong Chang's son Zhi in plotting to denounce the affair Zu had earlier reported, extorting a bribe from Yanling.

sentences.zh: 延齡執聰幽殺之，令聰子升焚其屍，而折所負券。

translations.literal: Yanling seized Cong, secretly killed him, had Cong's son Sheng burn the corpse, and tore up the debt note.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling seized Cong and secretly killed him, had Cong's son Sheng burn the body, and destroyed the debt note.

sentences.zh: 升噤不敢言，常憤詈至。

translations.literal: Sheng dared not speak out and often cursed Zhi in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng dared not speak out and often cursed Zhi in private fury.

sentences.zh: 至慮事發，乃摭聰前奏上之。

translations.literal: Zhi feared the affair would break out, so he gathered Si Cong's earlier memorial and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Zhi assembled Si Cong's earlier memorial and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 下刑部，逮延齡及諸奴雜治。

translations.literal: The case was sent down to the Ministry of Punishments; Yanling and his various slaves were arrested and jointly tried.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Ministry of Punishments; Yanling and his household slaves were arrested and tried together.

sentences.zh: 延齡嘗買沒官第宅，造園池，僭侈逾制。

translations.literal: Yanling had bought confiscated official residences and built gardens and ponds, extravagance exceeding regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling had purchased confiscated official residences and built gardens and ponds in extravagance that exceeded regulations.

sentences.zh: 又以私憾殺婢及僧，事並發覺。

translations.literal: He also killed a maidservant and a monk out of private resentment, and these matters all came to light together.
translations.idiomatic: He had also killed a maidservant and a monk out of private spite, and all these crimes came to light together.

sentences.zh: 刑部治延齡謀不軌，無驗，而違制殺人皆實，遂論死。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments tried Yanling for plotting treason but found no proof; yet his unauthorized killings were all substantiated, and he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments found no proof of Yanling's treason plot, but confirmed his unlawful killings, and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 系獄四年，獄囚劉東山發延齡手書訕上，東山得免戍，又陰構奸人劉琦誣延齡盜宮禁內帑，所告連數十百人。

translations.literal: After four years in prison, the prisoner Liu Dongshan produced Yanling's handwritten letters mocking the emperor; Dongshan won exemption from frontier exile, and covertly recruited the rogue Liu Qi to accuse Yanling of stealing from the palace treasury, implicating dozens or hundreds of people in the report.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in prison, the prisoner Liu Dongshan produced Yanling's handwritten letters mocking the emperor; Dongshan won exemption from frontier exile and covertly recruited the rogue Liu Qi to accuse Yanling of stealing from the palace treasury, implicating dozens or hundreds of people.

sentences.zh: 明年，奸人班期、於雲鶴又告延齡兄弟挾左道祝詛，辭及太后。

translations.literal: The next year the rogues Ban Qi and Yu Yunhe again reported that the Yanling brothers employed heterodox arts to curse and plot, their accusation implicating the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rogues Ban Qi and Yu Yunhe again reported that the Yanling brothers employed sorcery to curse and plot, implicating the empress dowager in their accusation.

sentences.zh: 鶴齡自南京赴逮，瘐死，期、雲鶴亦坐誣謫戍。

translations.literal: Heling came from Nanjing to answer the summons and died en route of illness; Qi and Yunhe were also convicted of false accusation and exiled to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Heling came from Nanjing to answer the summons and died en route of illness; Qi and Yunhe were also convicted of false accusation and exiled to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 又明年，東山以射父亡命，為御史陳讓所捕獲，復誣告延齡並構讓及遂安伯陳鏸等數十人，冀以悅上意而脫己罪。

translations.literal: The year after that, Dongshan, fleeing after killing his father, was captured by Censor Chen Rang; he again falsely accused Yanling and framed Rang and Marquis of Suian Chen Yi and dozens of others, hoping to please the emperor and escape his own guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Dongshan, fleeing after killing his father, was captured by Censor Chen Rang; he again falsely accused Yanling and framed Rang, Marquis of Suian Chen Yi, and dozens of others, hoping to please the emperor and escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 奏入，下錦衣衛窮治，讓獄中上疏言：「東山扇結奸黨，圖危宮禁。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the case was sent down to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for exhaustive investigation; from prison Rang submitted a memorial saying: "Dongshan has stirred up a faction of rogues and seeks to endanger the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the case was referred to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for exhaustive investigation; from prison Rang submitted a memorial saying, "Dongshan has stirred up a faction of rogues and seeks to endanger the palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下有帝堯既睦之德，而東山敢為陛下言漢武巫蠱之禍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the virtue of Emperor Yao in making kin harmonious, yet Dongshan dares tell Your Majesty of the witchcraft disaster of Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty possesses the virtue of Emperor Yao in making kin harmonious, yet Dongshan dares speak to Your Majesty of the witchcraft disaster of Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 陛下有帝爵底豫之孝，而東山敢導陛下以暴秦遷母之謀。

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the filial piety that delights the imperial parent, yet Dongshan dares guide Your Majesty toward the Qin tyrant's scheme of moving the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty possesses the filial piety that delights the imperial parent, yet Dongshan dares guide Your Majesty toward the Qin tyrant's scheme of displacing the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 離間骨肉，背逆不道，義不可赦。」

translations.literal: He drives a wedge between flesh and blood, rebels against the Way, and by right cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He drives a wedge between flesh and blood, rebels against the Way, and by right cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝頗悟。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor came partly to his senses.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor came partly to his senses.

sentences.zh: 指揮王佐典其獄，鉤得東山情，奏之。

translations.literal: Commander Wang Zuo oversaw the case, extracted Dongshan's motives, and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Zuo oversaw the case, extracted Dongshan's motives, and reported them.

sentences.zh: 乃械死東山，赦讓、鏸等，而延齡長系如故。

translations.literal: Dongshan was then executed in bonds; Rang, Yi, and the others were pardoned, while Yanling remained in long confinement as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dongshan was then executed in bonds; Rang, Yi, and the others were pardoned, while Yanling remained in long confinement as before.

sentences.zh: 太后崩之五年，延齡斬西市。

translations.literal: Five years after the empress dowager's death, Yanling was beheaded at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after the empress dowager's death, Yanling was beheaded at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 夏儒，毅皇后父也。

translations.literal: Xia Ru was the father of Empress Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Ru was the father of Empress Yi.

sentences.zh: 正德二年以後父封慶陽伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyang as the empress's father.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was enfeoffed as Earl of Qingyang as the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 為人長厚，父瑄疾，三年不去左右。

translations.literal: He was a man of generous character; when his father Xuan fell ill, he did not leave his side for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of generous character; when his father Xuan fell ill, he did not leave his side for three years.

sentences.zh: 既貴，服食如布衣時，見者不知為外戚也。

translations.literal: Once elevated, his dress and diet remained as in his commoner days, and those who saw him did not know he was an imperial in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated, his dress and diet remained as in his commoner days, and those who saw him did not know he was an imperial in-law.

sentences.zh: 十年以壽終，子臣嗣伯。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died of old age; his son Chen inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died of old age; his son Chen inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年罷襲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing the succession was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing the succession was abolished.

sentences.zh: 陳萬言，肅皇后父也，大名人，起家諸生。

translations.literal: Chen Wanyan was the father of Empress Su, a native of Daming who rose from the ranks of licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wanyan was the father of Empress Su, a native of Daming who rose from the ranks of licentiates.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年授鴻臚卿，改都督同知，賜第黃華坊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to vice commissioner-in-chief, and granted a residence in Huanghua Ward.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to vice commissioner-in-chief, and granted a residence in Huanghua Ward.

sentences.zh: 明年詔復營第於西安門外，費帑金數十萬。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered another residence built outside Xi'an Gate, costing several hundred thousand taels from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict ordered another residence built outside Xi'an Gate, costing several hundred thousand taels from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 工商尚書趙璜以西安門近大內，治第毋過高。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Huang said that Xi'an Gate was near the inner palace and the residence ought not be built too high.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Huang said that Xi'an Gate was near the inner palace and the residence ought not be built too high.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮營繕郎翟璘下獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and had Construction Director Zhai Lin imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and had Construction Director Zhai Lin imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 言官余瓚等諫，不省。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials including Yu Zan admonished him, but he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials including Yu Zan admonished him, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 尋封萬言泰和伯，子紹祖授尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: Soon Wanyan was enfeoffed as Earl of Taihe, and his son Shaozu was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Regalia Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wanyan was enfeoffed as Earl of Taihe, and his son Shaozu was appointed Assistant Director of the Imperial Regalia Office.

sentences.zh: 又明年，萬言乞武清、東安地各千頃為莊田，詔戶部勘閑地給之。

translations.literal: The year after that, Wanyan requested a thousand qing each in Wuqing and Dong'an as estate lands; an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to survey idle lands and grant them.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Wanyan requested a thousand qing each in Wuqing and Dong'an as estate lands; an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to survey idle lands and grant them.

sentences.zh: 給事中張漢卿言：「萬言拔跡儒素，聯婚天室，當躬自檢飭，為戚裏倡，而僭冒陳乞，違越法度。

translations.literal: Secretariat Receiver Zhang Hanqing said: "Wanyan rose from plain scholar stock and married into the imperial house; he ought to restrain himself and set an example among imperial in-laws, yet he presumptuously petitions and oversteps the law.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Receiver Zhang Hanqing said: "Wanyan rose from plain scholar stock and married into the imperial house; he ought to restrain himself and set an example among imperial in-laws, yet he presumptuously petitions and oversteps the law.

sentences.zh: 去歲深冬冱雪，急起大第，徒役疲勞，怨咨載道。

translations.literal: Last year, in deep winter with ice and snow, he hurriedly raised a great mansion; the laborers were worn out and complaint filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, in deep winter with ice and snow, he hurriedly raised a great mansion; the laborers were worn out and complaint filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 方今災沴相繼，江、淮餓死之人，掘穴掩埋，動以萬計。

translations.literal: At present disasters follow one after another; on the Yangtze and Huai, those who starved to death were buried in pits by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At present disasters follow one after another; on the Yangtze and Huai, those who starved to death were buried in pits by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 萬言曾不動念，益請莊田。

translations.literal: Wanyan gave no thought to this and instead asked for more estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan gave no thought to this and instead asked for more estate lands.

sentences.zh: 小民一廛一畝，終歲力作，猶不足於食，若又割而畀之貴戚，欲無流亡，不可得也。

translations.literal: For commoners, each homestead and each mu, worked through the year, still does not suffice for food; if more is carved away and given to the nobility, to hope for no flight from the land is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: For commoners, each homestead and each mu, worked through the year, still does not suffice for food; if more is carved away and given to the nobility, to hope for no flight from the land is impossible.

sentences.zh: 伏望割恩以義，杜漸以法，一切裁抑，令保延爵祿。」

translations.literal: We humbly beg that favor be cut according to justice, excess be stopped according to law, and everything be restrained, so that he may preserve his title and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg that favor be cut according to justice, excess be stopped according to law, and everything be restrained, so that he may preserve his title and stipend.

sentences.zh: 帝竟以八百頃給之。

translations.literal: The emperor still granted him eight hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still granted him eight hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉麟、御史任洛復言不宜奪民地，弗聽。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Lin and Censor Ren Luo again said it was improper to seize commoners' land, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Lin and Censor Ren Luo again said it was improper to seize commoners' land, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 七年，皇后崩，萬言亦絀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the empress died and Wanyan was also demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the empress died and Wanyan was also demoted.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒，子不得嗣封。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died; his son was not allowed to inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died; his son was not allowed to inherit the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 方銳，世宗孝烈皇后父也，應天人。

translations.literal: Fang Rui was the father of Empress Xiaolie of the Jiajing Emperor, a native of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Rui was the father of Empress Xiaolie of the Jiajing Emperor, a native of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 後初為九嬪，銳授錦衣正千戶。

translations.literal: When the consort was first one of the Nine Pin, Rui was appointed chief battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort was first one of the Nine Pin, Rui was appointed chief battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年，張後廢，後由妃冊為皇后，遷銳都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing Empress Zhang was deposed; the consort was raised from consort to empress, and Rui was transferred to chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing Empress Zhang was deposed; the consort was raised from consort to empress, and Rui was transferred to chief commander.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕南巡，道拜左都督。

translations.literal: While escorting the imperial tour to the south, he was en route made left commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the imperial tour to the south, he was en route made left commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 既封安平伯，尋進封侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Anping and soon advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Anping and soon raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，子承裕嗣。

translations.literal: At his death his son Chengyu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Chengyu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年用主事郭諫臣言，罷襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, on the recommendation of Section Chief Guo Jianchen, the succession was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing, on the recommendation of Section Chief Guo Jianchen, the succession was abolished.

sentences.zh: 李偉，字世奇，漷縣人，神宗生母李太后父也。

translations.literal: Li Wei, styled Shiqi, a native of Huo County, was the father of Empress Dowager Li, mother of the Shenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, styled Shiqi, a native of Huo County, was the father of Empress Dowager Li, mother of the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 兒時嬉里中，有羽士過之，驚語人曰：「此兒骨相，當位極人臣。」

translations.literal: As a child playing in the lane, a Taoist passed by and said in amazement to others: "This boy's bone structure shows he will rise to the highest rank among ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As a child playing in the lane, a Taoist passed by and said in amazement to others, "This boy's bone structure shows he will rise to the highest rank among ministers.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，偉夢空中五色彩輦，旌幢鼓吹導之下寢所，已而生太后。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era Wei dreamed of a five-colored imperial carriage in the sky, with banners, flags, and music escorting it down to his bedroom; afterward the empress dowager was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era Wei dreamed of a five-colored imperial carriage in the sky, with banners, flags, and music escorting it down to his bedroom; afterward the empress dowager was born.

sentences.zh: 避警，攜家入京師。

translations.literal: To avoid an imperial edict of arrest, he moved his family to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid an imperial edict of arrest, he moved his family to the capital.

sentences.zh: 居久之，太后入裕邸，生神宗。

translations.literal: After living there a long time, the empress dowager entered the Prince of Yu's residence and bore the Shenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After living there a long time, the empress dowager entered the Prince of Yu's residence and bore the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，立皇太子，授偉都督同知。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Longqing, when the crown prince was established, Wei was appointed vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the change of reign to Longqing, when the crown prince was established, Wei was appointed vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，封武清伯，再進武清侯。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor came to the throne, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Wuqing and then raised to Marquis of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli Emperor came to the throne, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Wuqing and then raised to Marquis of Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 太后能約束其家，偉嘗有過，太后召入宮切責之，不以父故骫祖宗法。

translations.literal: The empress dowager could restrain her family; when Wei once transgressed, she summoned him to the palace and sharply rebuked him, not bending ancestral law because he was her father.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager could restrain her family; when Wei once transgressed, she summoned him to the palace and sharply rebuked him, not bending ancestral law because he was her father.

sentences.zh: 以是，偉益小心畏慎，有賢聲。

translations.literal: For this reason Wei grew ever more cautious and careful, and gained a reputation for worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Wei grew ever more cautious and careful, and gained a reputation for worthiness.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年卒，贈安國公，謚莊簡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he died and was posthumously made Duke of Anguo, with the posthumous title Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Wanli he died and was posthumously made Duke of Anguo, with the posthumous title Zhuangjian, "Solemn and Simple."

sentences.zh: 子文全嗣侯，卒，子銘誠嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenquan inherited the marquisate; at his death his son Mingcheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenquan inherited the marquisate; at his death his son Mingcheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天啟末，銘誠頌魏忠賢功德，建祠名鴻勛。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianqi reign Mingcheng eulogized the merits of Wei Zhongxian and built a shrine named Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianqi reign Mingcheng eulogized the merits of Wei Zhongxian and built a shrine named Hongxun, "Great Merit."

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝定逆案，銘誠幸獲免。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor settled the list of traitors, Mingcheng fortunately escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor settled the list of traitors, Mingcheng fortunately escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 久之，大學士薛國觀請勒勛戚助軍餉。

translations.literal: After a long time Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan asked that imperial in-laws be compelled to aid military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan asked that imperial in-laws be compelled to aid military provisions.

sentences.zh: 時銘誠已卒，子國瑞當嗣爵，其庶兄國臣與爭產，言父遺貲四十萬，願輸以佐軍興。

translations.literal: By then Mingcheng had died; his son Guorui was due to inherit the title, but his elder brother by a concubine, Guochen, disputed the estate, saying their father had left four hundred thousand in assets and offering to contribute them to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mingcheng had died; his son Guorui was due to inherit the title, but his elder brother by a concubine, Guochen, disputed the estate, saying their father had left four hundred thousand in assets and offering to contribute them to aid the army.

sentences.zh: 帝初不允，至是詔借餉如國臣言，國瑞不能應。

translations.literal: The emperor at first refused, but now issued an edict to borrow provisions as Guochen said; Guorui could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first refused, but now issued an edict to borrow provisions as Guochen said; Guorui could not comply.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪國瑞爵，遂悸死，有司復系其家人。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, stripped Guorui of his title, and Guorui died of fright; the authorities again seized his family members.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, stripped Guorui of his title, and Guorui died of fright; the authorities again seized his family members.

sentences.zh: 國瑞女字嘉定伯周奎孫，奎請於莊烈後，後曰：「但迎女，秋毫無所取可也。」

translations.literal: Guorui's daughter was betrothed to a grandson of Marquis of Jiading Zhou Kui; Kui asked the Chongzhen Empress, and the empress said: "Only welcome the daughter—take not the slightest thing besides.
translations.idiomatic: Guorui's daughter was betrothed to a grandson of Marquis of Jiading Zhou Kui; Kui asked the Chongzhen Empress, and the empress said, "Only welcome the daughter—take not the slightest thing besides.

sentences.zh: 諸戚畹人人自危。

translations.literal: Every imperial in-law was thrown into fear for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Every imperial in-law was thrown into fear for himself.

sentences.zh: 會皇五子疾亟，李太后憑而言。

translations.literal: When the fifth imperial son fell dangerously ill, Empress Dowager Li spoke leaning on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifth imperial son fell dangerously ill, Empress Dowager Li spoke leaning on him.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，悉還李氏產，復武清爵，而皇五子竟殤。

translations.literal: The emperor was afraid, fully restored the Li family's property, and revived the Wuqing title—but the fifth imperial son still died young.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was afraid, fully restored the Li family's property, and revived the Wuqing title—but the fifth imperial son still died young.

sentences.zh: 或云中人構乳媼，教皇五子言之也。

translations.literal: Some said palace eunuchs had coached the wet nurse to teach the fifth imperial son to say it.
translations.idiomatic: Some said palace eunuchs had coached the wet nurse to teach the fifth imperial son to say it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，國觀遂以事誅。

translations.literal: Before long Xue Guoguan was executed on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xue Guoguan was executed on another charge.

sentences.zh: 王偉，神宗顯皇后父也。

translations.literal: Wang Wei was the father of Empress Xian of the Shenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei was the father of Empress Xian of the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年授都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he was appointed commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli he was appointed commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋封永年伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加恩偉子棟及其弟俊，閣臣請俱授錦衣正千戶。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to extend favor to Wei's son Dong and his younger brother Jun; the grand secretaries asked that both be appointed chief battalion commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to extend favor to Wei's son Dong and his younger brother Jun; the grand secretaries asked that both be appointed chief battalion commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「正德時，皇親夏助等俱授錦衣指揮使，世襲，今何薄也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Under Zhengde, imperial kinsmen such as Xia Zhu were all appointed commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with hereditary succession—why so meager now?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Under Zhengde, imperial kinsmen such as Xia Zhu were all appointed commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard with hereditary succession—why so meager now?

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正等言：「正德時例，世宗悉已厘革，請授棟錦衣衛指揮僉事，俊千戶，如前議。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and others said: "The precedents of the Zhengde era were all rectified by the Jiajing Emperor; we ask that Dong be appointed assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and Jun a battalion commander, as previously proposed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and others said, "The precedents of the Zhengde era were all rectified by the Jiajing Emperor; we ask that Dong be appointed assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and Jun a battalion commander, as previously proposed."

sentences.zh: 帝意未慊，居正固奏，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was still displeased; Juzheng pressed his memorial and only then did he desist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still displeased; Juzheng pressed his memorial and only then did he desist.

sentences.zh: 偉卒，傳子棟及曾孫明輔，襲伯如制。

translations.literal: When Wei died, the title passed to his son Dong and then to his great-grandson Mingfu, who inherited the earldom according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei died, the title passed to his son Dong and then to his great-grandson Mingfu, who inherited the earldom according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 鄭承憲，神宗鄭貴妃父也。

translations.literal: Zheng Chengxian was the father of Consort Zheng of the Shenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chengxian was the father of Consort Zheng of the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 貴妃有寵，鄭氏父子、宗族並驕恣，帝悉不問。

translations.literal: As the consort held favor, the Zheng father and son and their entire clan grew arrogant and unrestrained, yet the emperor asked nothing of them.
translations.idiomatic: As the consort held favor, the Zheng father and son and their entire clan grew arrogant and unrestrained, yet the emperor asked nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 承憲累官至都督同知，卒。

translations.literal: Chengxian rose through posts to vice commissioner-in-chief and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxian rose through posts to vice commissioner-in-chief and died.

sentences.zh: 子國泰請襲，帝命授都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Guotai asked to inherit; the emperor ordered him made chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guotai asked to inherit; the emperor ordered him made chief commander.

sentences.zh: 給事中張希臯言：「指揮使下都督一等，不宜授任子。

translations.literal: Secretariat Receiver Zhang Xigao said: "Assistant commander ranks one grade below commissioner-in-chief—it is not fitting to grant that post to a son.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Receiver Zhang Xigao said, "Assistant commander ranks one grade below commissioner-in-chief—it is not fitting to grant that post to a son.

sentences.zh: 妃家蒙恩如是，何以優後家。」

translations.literal: If the consort's family is favored so, how can the empress's family be honored?
translations.idiomatic: If the consort's family is favored so, how can the empress's family be honored?

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 是時，廷臣疑貴妃謀奪嫡，群以為言。

translations.literal: At that time court officials suspected the consort of plotting to supplant the heir apparent, and spoke out in groups.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court officials suspected the consort of plotting to supplant the heir apparent, and spoke out in groups.

sentences.zh: 國泰不自安，上疏請立太子，其從子承恩亦言儲位不宜久虛。

translations.literal: Guotai grew uneasy and submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince be established; his nephew Chengen also said the succession ought not remain vacant long.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai grew uneasy and submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince be established; his nephew Chengen also said the succession ought not remain vacant long.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫左右於帝，弗聽。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan sided with the emperor at court and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan sided with the emperor at court and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 詔奪國泰俸，而斥承恩為民，然言者終不息。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Guotai of his stipend and reduced Chengen to commoner status, yet the speakers still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Guotai of his stipend and reduced Chengen to commoner status, yet the speakers still did not cease.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年，承恩復上疏劾給事中戴士衡、知縣樊玉衡，妄造《憂危竑議》，離間骨肉，汙蔑皇貴妃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli Chengen again submitted a memorial impeaching Secretariat Receiver Dai Shiheng and Magistrate Fan Yuheng for fabricating the "Pavilion of Shared Peril" pamphlet, driving a wedge between flesh and blood and slandering the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli Chengen again submitted a memorial impeaching Secretariat Receiver Dai Shiheng and Magistrate Fan Yuheng for fabricating the "Pavilion of Shared Peril" pamphlet, driving a wedge between flesh and blood and slandering the Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 《憂危竑議》者，不知誰所作，中言侍郎呂坤構通宮掖，將與國泰等擁戴福王。

translations.literal: The "Pavilion of Shared Peril" pamphlet was by an unknown author; it said Vice Minister Lu Kun had conspired with the palace women's quarters and would join Guotai and others in enthroning the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The "Pavilion of Shared Peril" pamphlet was by an unknown author; it said Vice Minister Lu Kun had conspired with the palace women's quarters and would join Guotai and others in enthroning the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 而士衡前嘗論坤與承恩相結，玉衡方抗言貴妃沮立太子，疏並留中，故承恩指兩人。
