translations.literal: Shiheng had earlier argued that Kun and Chengen were in league; Yuheng had just boldly said the consort was obstructing establishment of the crown prince—their memorials had both been held at court—so Chengen pointed at the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng had earlier argued that Kun and Chengen were in league; Yuheng had just boldly said the consort was obstructing establishment of the crown prince—their memorials had both been held at court—so Chengen pointed at the two men.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，士衡、玉衡皆永戍。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; Shiheng and Yuheng were both exiled in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; Shiheng and Yuheng were both exiled in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 廷臣益貧鄭氏。

translations.literal: Court officials treated the Zheng clan with ever greater contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials treated the Zheng clan with ever greater contempt.

sentences.zh: 久之，皇太子立。

translations.literal: After a long time the crown prince was established.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time the crown prince was established.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，男子張差持梃入東宮，被擒。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year a man named Zhang Cha entered the Eastern Palace wielding a club and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year a man named Zhang Cha entered the Eastern Palace wielding a club and was seized.

sentences.zh: 言者皆言國泰謀刺皇太子。

translations.literal: Speakers all said Guotai had plotted to assassinate the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Speakers all said Guotai had plotted to assassinate the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 主事王之寀鞫差，差指貴妃宮監。

translations.literal: Section Chief Wang Zhicai interrogated Cha; Cha pointed to a eunuch of the consort's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Section Chief Wang Zhicai interrogated Cha; Cha pointed to a eunuch of the consort's palace.

sentences.zh: 主事陸大受、給事中何士晉遂直攻國泰。

translations.literal: Section Chief Lu Dashou and Secretariat Receiver He Shijin then directly attacked Guotai.
translations.idiomatic: Section Chief Lu Dashou and Secretariat Receiver He Shijin then pressed their attack on Guotai without restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝以貴妃故，不欲竟事，詳之寀等傳。

translations.literal: Because of the Noble Consort, the emperor did not wish to pursue the matter to the end; the details are in the biographies of Zhicai and others.
translations.idiomatic: For the Noble Consort's sake the emperor would not see the case through; particulars appear in the biographies of Zhicai and others.

sentences.zh: 國泰官左都督，病死，子養性襲職。

translations.literal: Guotai held the post of Left Commissioner-in-Chief; he died of illness, and his son Yangxing inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai served as Left Commissioner-in-Chief, died of illness, and was succeeded by his son Yangxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，光祿少卿高攀龍、御史陳必謙追論其罪，且言養性結白蓮賊將為亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Gao Panlong and Censor Chen Biqian reviewed his crimes and also said Yangxing had joined White Lotus bandit generals to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Gao Panlong and Censor Chen Biqian reopened the case against him and charged that Yangxing had allied with White Lotus rebel commanders to foment disorder.

sentences.zh: 詔勒養性出京師，隨便居住。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yangxing to leave the capital and reside wherever he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded Yangxing to quit the capital and live wherever he chose.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢用事，宥還。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian held power, he was pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Zhongxian came to power, Yangxing was pardoned and permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 王升，熹宗生母孝和太后弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xiaohe, birth mother of the Tianqi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Xiaohe, mother of the Tianqi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 父鉞。

translations.literal: His father was Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yue.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年封升新城伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, Sheng was enfeoffed as Earl of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi, Sheng received the title Earl of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 尋以皇子生，進俟。

translations.literal: Soon after, because an imperial son was born, he was promoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when an imperial son was born, he was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，子國興嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Guoxing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Guoxing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年，京師陷，被殺。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, when the capital fell, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, when the capital fell, he was slain.

sentences.zh: 劉文炳，字淇筠，宛平人。

translations.literal: Liu Wenbing, styled Qijun, was a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenbing, styled Qijun, came from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 祖應元，娶徐氏，生女，入宮，即莊烈帝生母孝純皇太后也。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingyuan married the Xu clan and had a daughter who entered the palace—she was Empress Dowager Xiaochun, birth mother of the Chongzhen Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingyuan married a woman of the Xu clan; their daughter entered the palace and became Empress Dowager Xiaochun, mother of the Chongzhen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 應元早卒，帝即位，封太后弟效祖新樂伯，即文炳父也。

translations.literal: Yingyuan died early; when the emperor ascended the throne, he enfeoffed the empress dowager's younger brother Xiaozu as Earl of Xinle—he was Wenbing's father.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan died young; when the emperor took the throne he enfeoffed the empress dowager's younger brother Xiaozu as Earl of Xinle—Wenbing's father.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年卒，文炳嗣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen he died; Wenbing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Chongzhen, and Wenbing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 是年，文炳大母徐年七十，賜寶鈔、白金、文綺。

translations.literal: That year Wenbing's grandmother Xu turned seventy; she was granted treasure notes, silver, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Wenbing's grandmother, Lady Xu, turned seventy and was granted treasure notes, silver, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 帝謂內侍曰：「太夫人年老，猶聰明善飯，使太后在，不知若何稱壽也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the palace attendants: "The Lady is advanced in years, yet still clear-minded and hearty in her eating—if the empress dowager were alive, one knows not how we would celebrate her longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the palace attendants, "The Lady is old, yet still sharp of mind and hearty at table—had the empress dowager lived, who knows what a birthday celebration we might have held.

sentences.zh: 因愴然泣下。

translations.literal: He then wept in deep sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He then broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 九年進文炳為新樂侯，其祖、父世贈爵如之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wenbing was promoted to Marquis of Xinle; his grandfather and father received posthumous ennoblements to matching ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Wenbing was raised to Marquis of Xinle, and his grandfather and father were posthumously ennobled to corresponding ranks.

sentences.zh: 十三年，宮中奉太后像，或曰未肖。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the palace displayed a portrait of the empress dowager; some said it was not lifelike.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the palace installed a portrait of the empress dowager, but some said it did not resemble her.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，遣司禮監太監王裕民同武英殿中書至文炳第，敕徐口授，繪像以進，左右鹹驚曰：「肖。」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he sent Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Wang Yumin together with a drafting secretary of the Hall of Military Glory to Wenbing's residence, ordering Lady Xu to dictate from memory, and had a portrait painted and submitted. Those on either side all exclaimed in astonishment: "It is lifelike.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and sent Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Wang Yumin, together with a drafting secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, to Wenbing's house, where Lady Xu was ordered to describe her daughter's features from memory. When the portrait was submitted, all those present cried out in amazement: "It is her likeness.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，命卜日具鹵簿，帝俯伏歸極門，迎入，安奉奉慈殿，朝夕上食如生。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; he ordered an auspicious day chosen and full imperial escort prepared. The emperor prostrated himself at the Gate of Ultimate Rest and welcomed the portrait in; it was installed in the Hall of Cherishing Kindness, and morning and evening offerings were made as though she were alive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed. He chose an auspicious day, assembled the full imperial escort, prostrated himself at the Gate of Ultimate Rest to welcome the portrait, and installed it in the Hall of Cherishing Kindness, where morning and evening offerings were served as though she still lived.

sentences.zh: 因追贈應元瀛國公，封徐氏瀛國太夫人，文炳晉少傅，叔繼祖，弟文燿、文照俱晉爵有差。

translations.literal: Accordingly Yingyuan was posthumously ennobled Duke of Ying, Lady Xu was enfeoffed as Lady of Ying, Wenbing was promoted to Junior Mentor, his uncle Jizu and younger brothers Wenyao and Wenzhao all received promotions of varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan was posthumously ennobled Duke of Ying, Lady Xu was enfeoffed Lady of Ying, Wenbing was promoted to Junior Mentor, and his uncle Jizu and younger brothers Wenyao and Wenzhao all received titles of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 文炳母杜氏賢，每謂文炳等曰：「吾家無功德，直以太后故，受此大恩，當盡忠報天子。」

translations.literal: Wenbing's mother, the worthy Lady Du, often said to Wenbing and the others: "Our house has no merit; we received this great favor solely because of the empress dowager. We must serve the Son of Heaven with full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing's mother, the virtuous Lady Du, often told Wenbing and his brothers, "Our family has no merit of its own; we owe this great favor only to the empress dowager. We must repay the emperor with absolute loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝遣文炳視鳳陽祖陵，密諭有大事上聞。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wenbing to inspect the ancestral tombs at Fengyang, secretly instructing him to report any major matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wenbing to inspect the imperial tombs at Fengyang and secretly instructed him to report anything of grave importance.

sentences.zh: 文炳歸，奏史可法、張國維忠正有方略，宜久任，必能滅賊，後兩人果殉國難。

translations.literal: When Wenbing returned, he memorialized that Shi Kefa and Zhang Guowei were loyal, upright, and resourceful, and should be kept in office long—they would surely destroy the bandits. Later both men indeed died for the realm in its crisis.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Wenbing memorialized that Shi Kefa and Zhang Guowei were loyal, upright, and capable, and should be kept in office long enough to destroy the rebels. Both men later died defending the realm.

sentences.zh: 文炳謹厚不妄交，獨與宛平太學生申湛然、布衣黃尼麓及駙馬都尉鞏永固善。

translations.literal: Wenbing was careful and steady and did not associate casually; he was close only to Wanping Imperial Academy student Shen Zhanran, commoner Huang Nilu, and Commandant-in-Chief Gong Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing was cautious and reserved in his friendships, associating closely only with Wanping Imperial Academy student Shen Zhanran, commoner Huang Nilu, and Commandant-in-Chief Gong Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 時天下多故，流賊勢益張，文炳與民麓等講明忠義，為守禦計。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was beset by troubles and bandit strength grew ever greater; Wenbing together with Nilu and others expounded loyalty and righteousness and made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm fell into turmoil and rebel power swelled, Wenbing and Nilu and their circle studied loyalty and righteousness and laid plans for the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 及李自成據三秦，破榆林，將犯京師。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng held the Three Qins, captured Yulin, and was about to strike the capital—
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized the Three Qins, broke Yulin, and prepared to march on the capital—

sentences.zh: 文炳知勢不支，慷慨泣下，謂永固曰：「國事至此，我與公受國恩，當以死報。」

translations.literal: Wenbing knew the situation could not be sustained; weeping with righteous grief, he said to Yonggu: "Affairs of state have come to this. You and I have received the state's grace—we must repay it with our lives."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the cause was lost, Wenbing wept with fierce resolve and told Yonggu, "Affairs have come to this pass. You and I have received the state's grace—we must repay it with our lives."

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，帝召文炳、永固等回國事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year the emperor summoned Wenbing, Yonggu, and others to discuss state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year the emperor summoned Wenbing, Yonggu, and others to counsel him on the state of the realm.

sentences.zh: 二人請早建藩封，遣永、定二王之國。

translations.literal: The two men asked that enfeoffments be established early and the Princes of Yong and Ding be sent to their fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The two urged that the princes be enfeoffed without delay and that the Princes of Yong and Ding be dispatched to their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 帝是之，以內帑乏，不果行。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, but because the inner treasury was depleted, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed in principle, but the inner treasury was empty and the plan never went forward.

sentences.zh: 三月初一日，賊警益急，命文武勛戚分守京城。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month bandit alarms grew ever more urgent; the emperor ordered civil and military officials, meritorious peers, and imperial kinsmen each to hold part of the capital in defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month rebel alarms grew acute, and the emperor ordered civil and military officials, meritorious peers, and imperial kinsmen to divide the defense of the capital among them.

sentences.zh: 繼祖守皇城東安門，文燿守永定門，永固守崇文門。

translations.literal: Jizu guarded the Imperial City's East Pacification Gate, Wenyao the Everlasting Stability Gate, and Yonggu the Reverence for Culture Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu held the Imperial City's East Pacification Gate, Wenyao the Everlasting Stability Gate, and Yonggu the Reverence for Culture Gate.

sentences.zh: 文炳以繼祖、文燿皆守城，故未有職事。

translations.literal: Because Jizu and Wenyao were both defending the walls, Wenbing had no assigned post.
translations.idiomatic: With Jizu and Wenyao both assigned to the walls, Wenbing had no post of his own.

sentences.zh: 十六日，賊攻西直門，勢益急。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth the bandits attacked the Direct Gate; the situation grew ever more critical.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth the rebels assaulted the Direct Gate, and the crisis deepened.

sentences.zh: 尼麓踉蹌至，謂文炳曰：「城將陷，君宜自為計。」

translations.literal: Nilu came stumbling up and said to Wenbing: "The city is about to fall—you should look to your own plan.
translations.idiomatic: Nilu came stumbling in and told Wenbing, "The city is about to fall—you must decide what to do for yourself.

sentences.zh: 文炳母杜氏聞之，即命侍婢簡笥絳於樓上，作七八繯，命家僮積薪樓下，隨遣老仆鄭平迎李氏、吳氏二女歸，曰：「吾母女同死此。」

translations.literal: When Wenbing's mother Lady Du heard this, she immediately ordered her maidservants to pick silk-sash cords upstairs and make seven or eight nooses; she had household servants pile firewood below the tower, then sent the old servant Zheng Ping to bring back the two daughters of the Li and Wu clans, saying: "We mothers and daughters shall die together here."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing's mother, Lady Du, heard this, she at once had her maidservants choose silk cords upstairs and knot seven or eight nooses, ordered the servants to pile firewood below the tower, and sent the old retainer Zheng Ping to fetch the two daughters of the Li and Wu families, saying, "We mothers and daughters shall die together here."

sentences.zh: 又念瀛國太夫人年篤老，不可俱燼，因與文炳計，匿之申湛然家。

translations.literal: She also reflected that the Lady of Ying was very aged and could not be consumed in the flames together with them; she therefore planned with Wenbing to hide her at Shen Zhanran's home.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that the Lady of Ying was very old and could not be burned with them, she and Wenbing arranged to hide her at Shen Zhanran's house.

sentences.zh: 十八日，帝遣內使密召文炳、永固。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth the emperor secretly sent palace envoys to summon Wenbing and Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth the emperor secretly dispatched palace envoys to summon Wenbing and Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 文炳歸白母曰：「有詔召兒，兒不能事母。」

translations.literal: Wenbing returned and told his mother: "There is an edict summoning your son—I cannot wait upon you, Mother.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing went home and told his mother, "There is an edict summoning me—I can no longer serve you, Mother.

sentences.zh: 母拊文炳背曰：「太夫人既得所，我與若妻妹死耳，復何憾。」

translations.literal: His mother patted Wenbing's back and said: "The Lady already has a safe place; I and your wife and sisters need only die—what regret remains?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother patted his back and said, "The Lady is already safe; I and your wife and sisters need only die—what more is there to regret?"

sentences.zh: 文炳偕永固謁帝，時外城已陷。

translations.literal: Wenbing went with Yonggu to audience with the emperor; by then the outer city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing and Yonggu went to audience with the emperor; by then the outer city had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「二卿所糾家丁，能巷戰否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The household troops you have mustered—can they fight in the lanes?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "The household troops you have gathered—can they fight in the streets?

sentences.zh: 文炳以眾寡不敵對，帝愕然。

translations.literal: Wenbing replied that they were too few to match the enemy; the emperor was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing answered that they were too few to stand against the enemy, and the emperor was stricken.

sentences.zh: 永固奏曰：「臣等已積薪第中，當闔門焚死，以報皇上。」

translations.literal: Yonggu submitted: "We have already piled firewood in our mansions; we shall burn our entire households to death to repay Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu submitted, "We have already piled firewood in our mansions and shall burn our whole households to death to repay Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕誌決矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My resolve is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 朕不能守社稷，朕能死社稷。」

translations.literal: I cannot preserve the altars of soil and grain—but I can die for them."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot preserve the altars of state, but I can die for them."

sentences.zh: 兩人皆涕泣誓效死，出馳至崇文門。

translations.literal: Both men wept, swore to give their lives, went out and galloped to the Reverence for Culture Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Both men wept, swore to die in service, rode out, and galloped to the Reverence for Culture Gate.

sentences.zh: 須臾賊大至，永固射賊，文炳助之，殺數十人，各馳歸第。

translations.literal: In a moment the bandits arrived in force; Yonggu shot at them and Wenbing aided him, killing several dozen men; each then galloped back to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels arrived in force. Yonggu shot at them and Wenbing fought beside him, killing several dozen men; then each galloped back to his own house.

sentences.zh: 十九日，文照方侍母飯，家人急入曰：「城陷矣！」

translations.literal: On the nineteenth Wenzhao was just attending his mother at meal when a servant rushed in saying: "The city has fallen!
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth Wenzhao was serving his mother at table when a servant burst in crying, "The city has fallen!

sentences.zh: 文照碗脫地，直視母。

translations.literal: Wenzhao's bowl fell to the floor; he looked straight at his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao's bowl dropped to the floor, and he looked straight at his mother.

sentences.zh: 母遽起登樓，文照及二女從之，文炳妻王氏亦登樓。

translations.literal: His mother rose at once and went up the tower; Wenzhao and the two daughters followed, and Wenbing's wife Lady Wang also went up.
translations.idiomatic: His mother rose at once and climbed the tower; Wenzhao and the two daughters followed, and Wenbing's wife, Lady Wang, went up as well.

sentences.zh: 懸孝純皇太后像，母率眾哭拜，各縊死。

translations.literal: They hung a portrait of Empress Dowager Xiaochun; the mother led all in weeping and obeisance, and each hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: They hung a portrait of Empress Dowager Xiaochun; the mother led them in weeping and obeisance, and each hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 文照入繯墮，拊母背連呼曰：「兒不能死矣，從母命，留侍太夫人。」

translations.literal: Wenzhao entered the noose but fell; he patted his mother's back and cried repeatedly: "Your son cannot die—I follow Mother's command and remain to attend the Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao put his head in the noose but fell; he patted his mother's back and cried again and again, "Your son cannot die—I obey Mother's command and remain to serve the Lady.

sentences.zh: 遂逃去。

translations.literal: He then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fled.

sentences.zh: 家人共焚樓。

translations.literal: The household together set the tower ablaze.
translations.idiomatic: The household together set fire to the tower.

sentences.zh: 文炳歸，火烈不得入，入後園，適湛然、尼麓至，曰：「鞏都尉已焚府第，自刎矣。」

translations.literal: Wenbing returned; the fire was fierce and he could not enter; he went into the rear garden. Just then Zhanran and Nilu arrived and said: "Commandant Gong has already burned his mansion and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing returned, but the flames were too fierce to enter; he went into the rear garden. Just then Zhanran and Nilu arrived and said, "Commandant Gong has already burned his mansion and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 文炳曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Wenbing said: "So be it."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing said, "So be it."

sentences.zh: 將投井，忽止曰：「戎服也，不可見皇帝。」

translations.literal: About to throw himself into a well, he suddenly stopped and said: "I am in military dress—it would not do to appear before the emperor thus."
translations.idiomatic: About to throw himself into the well, he suddenly stopped and said, "I am in armor—I cannot appear before the emperor like this."

sentences.zh: 湛然脫己幘冠之，遂投井死。

translations.literal: Zhanran removed his own headcloth and capped him with it; Wenbing then threw himself into the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanran removed his own headcloth and put it on Wenbing's head; Wenbing then threw himself into the well and died.

sentences.zh: 繼祖歸，亦投井死。

translations.literal: Jizu returned and likewise threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu returned and likewise threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 繼祖妻左氏見大宅火，亟登樓自焚，妾董氏、李氏亦焚死。

translations.literal: Jizu's wife Lady Zuo, seeing the great mansion afire, hurried up the tower and burned herself; the concubines Ladies Dong and Li also burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu's wife, Lady Zuo, seeing the great house in flames, hurried upstairs and burned herself; concubines Lady Dong and Lady Li burned to death as well.

sentences.zh: 初，文燿見外城破，突出至渾河，聞內城破，復入，見第焚，大哭曰：「文燿未死，以君與母在。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenyao saw the outer city breached, he broke out and reached the Hun River; hearing the inner city had fallen, he returned, saw the mansion burning, and wept loudly: "Wenyao did not die because His Majesty and Mother were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wenyao saw the outer city fall, he broke out as far as the Hun River; hearing that the inner city too had fallen, he returned, saw the mansion burning, and wept aloud, "Wenyao did not die because the emperor and Mother were still alive.

sentences.zh: 今至此，何生為！」

translations.literal: Now that it has come to this—what reason is there to live!
translations.idiomatic: Now that it has come to this—what reason is there to live!

sentences.zh: 遂覓文炳死所，大書版井旁曰「左都督劉文燿同兄文炳畢命報國處」，亦投井死，闔門死者四十二人。

translations.literal: He then sought the place where Wenbing had died, wrote on a board beside the well in large characters "Here Left Commissioner Liu Wenyao with his elder brother Wenbing gave their lives to repay the realm," and also threw himself into the well and died. Forty-two people of the household died in all.
translations.idiomatic: He then found the place where Wenbing had died, wrote on a board beside the well in large characters, "Here Left Commissioner Liu Wenyao and his elder brother Wenbing gave their lives for the realm," and threw himself into the well as well. Forty-two members of the household died in all.

sentences.zh: 是時，惠安伯張慶臻集妻子同焚死。

translations.literal: At that time Earl of Huian Zhang Qingzhen gathered wife and children and burned together to death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Earl of Huian Zhang Qingzhen gathered his wife and children and burned with them to death.

sentences.zh: 新城侯王國興亦焚死。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xincheng Wang Guoxing also burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Xincheng Wang Guoxing also burned to death.

sentences.zh: 宣城伯衛時春懷鐵券，闔門赴井死。

translations.literal: Earl of Xuancheng Wei Shichun, clutching his iron covenant tablet, led his entire household to the wells and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earl of Xuancheng Wei Shichun, clutching his iron covenant tablet, led his entire household to the wells and died together.

sentences.zh: 與永固射賊楊光陛者，駙馬都尉子也，被甲馳突左右射，與永固相失，矢盡，投觀象臺下井中死。

translations.literal: Yang Guangbi, who had shot at bandits alongside Yonggu, was the son of a Commandant-in-Chief; clad in armor he charged and shot left and right, lost contact with Yonggu, exhausted his arrows, and threw himself into the well beneath the Observatory Platform and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangbi, who had fought beside Yonggu shooting at the rebels, was the son of a Commandant-in-Chief. Clad in armor he charged and shot on every side, lost contact with Yonggu, exhausted his arrows, and threw himself into the well beneath the Observatory Platform and died.

sentences.zh: 而湛然以匿瀛國為賊所拷掠，終不言，體糜爛以死。

translations.literal: Zhanran, for having hidden the Lady of Ying, was tortured by the bandits; to the end he would not speak, and his body was broken and torn until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanran, for having hidden the Lady of Ying, was tortured by the rebels; he never spoke, and his body was torn apart until he died.

sentences.zh: 福王時，謚文炳忠壯，文燿忠果。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Wenbing was given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang and Wenyao Zhongguo.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Wenbing was posthumously titled Loyal and Stalwart and Wenyao Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 張國紀，祥符人，熹宗張皇后父也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoji, a native of Xiangfu, was the father of Empress Zhang of the Tianqi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoji, a native of Xiangfu, was the father of Empress Zhang, consort of the Tianqi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，封太康伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was enfeoffed as Earl of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was enfeoffed Earl of Taikang.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢與客氏忌皇后，因謀陷國紀，使其黨劉誌選、梁夢環先後劾國紀謀占宮婢韋氏，矯中宮旨鬻獄。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian and Ke Shi resented the empress and therefore plotted to entrap Guoji, having their partisans Liu Zhixuan and Liang Menghuan successively impeach Guoji for scheming to seize the palace maid Wei and sell pardons by forging orders in the empress's name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian and Ke Shi resented the empress and plotted to ruin Guoji, sending their partisans Liu Zhixuan and Liang Menghuan to impeach him in turn for scheming to take possession of the palace maid Wei and sell pardons by forging the empress's orders.

sentences.zh: 忠賢將從中究其事，以撼後。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was about to investigate the matter from within to shake the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian intended to pursue the case from within the palace in order to undermine the empress.

sentences.zh: 大學士李國𣚴曰：「君後，猶父母也，安有勸父構母者？」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Guozhen said: "The ruler and empress are like father and mother—how could there be one who urges a father to plot against a mother?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Guozhen said, "The emperor and empress are like father and mother—who would urge a father to plot against a mother?

sentences.zh: 國紀始放歸故郡，忠賢猶欲掎之，莊烈帝立，乃得免。

translations.literal: Guoji was first sent back to his native district; Zhongxian still wished to pull him down, but when the Chongzhen Emperor ascended he was finally spared.
translations.idiomatic: Guoji was first sent back to his home district; Zhongxian still sought to bring him down, but once the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne he was spared.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，以輸餉進爵為侯，旋死於賊。

translations.literal: In the late Chongzhen period he was promoted to marquis for contributing military funds, and soon died at the hands of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Chongzhen reign he was raised to marquis for contributing military funds, and soon died at rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 周奎，蘇州人，莊烈帝周皇后父也。

translations.literal: Zhou Kui, a native of Suzhou, was the father of Empress Zhou of the Chongzhen Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kui, a native of Suzhou, was the father of Empress Zhou, consort of the Chongzhen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年封嘉定伯，賜第於蘇州之葑門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiading and granted a mansion at Suzhou's Feng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jiading and granted a mansion at the Feng Gate in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭奎及田貴妃父弘遇、袁貴妃父祐，宜恪遵法度，為諸戚臣先。

translations.literal: The emperor once admonished Kui together with Tian Consort's father Hongyu and Yuan Consort's father You that they should strictly observe the law and be foremost among all kinsmen in setting an example.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once admonished Kui, together with Tian Consort's father Hongyu and Yuan Consort's father You, to observe the law strictly and set an example for all imperial kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 祐頗謹慎，惟弘遇驕縱，奎居外戚中，碌碌而已。

translations.literal: You was quite careful; only Hongyu was proud and unrestrained. Among the empress's kinsmen Kui was merely ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: You was cautious and restrained; only Hongyu was proud and unrestrained. Among the empress's kinsmen, Kui was unremarkable.

sentences.zh: 李自成逼京師，帝遣內侍徐高密諭奎倡勛戚輸餉，奎堅謝無有。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng pressed the capital, the emperor sent palace attendant Xu Gao secretly to instruct Kui to take the lead among meritorious kinsmen in contributing military funds; Kui firmly declined, saying he had none.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng pressed the capital, the emperor sent palace attendant Xu Gao secretly to urge Kui to lead the meritorious kinsmen in contributing military funds; Kui firmly refused, insisting he had nothing to give.

sentences.zh: 高憤泣曰：「後父如此，國事去矣。」

translations.literal: Gao wept in anger and said: "When the empress's father is like this, the realm's cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gao wept in anger and said, "When the empress's father behaves like this, the realm is lost.

sentences.zh: 奎不得已奏捐萬金，且乞皇后為助。

translations.literal: Kui had no choice but to memorialize a donation of ten thousand in gold, and also begged the empress to help.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had no choice but to memorialize a donation of ten thousand taels of gold and also beg the empress for assistance.

sentences.zh: 及自成陷京師，掠其家得金數萬計，人以是笑奎之愚雲。

translations.literal: When Zicheng captured the capital, loot from his household yielded tens of thousands in gold; people therefore laughed at Kui's folly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng captured the capital, loot from his household yielded tens of thousands in gold, and people laughed at Kui's folly.
